rows.name: Aakanksha Sharma
lines: I’m a Principal at General Catalyst - India, a global investment and transformation company that partners with the world’s most ambitious entrepreneurs to drive resilience and applied AI. At GC, I invest in fintech and consumer companies across stages.

I bring about 12 years of experience in the Indian investing and financial services domain. Before joining GC, I was a Principal at Venture Highway (a seed-stage fund) and a VP at IvyCap Ventures (a Series A/B focused fund).

My journey as an investor began with an internship at Samara Capital, a mid-market private equity firm. I started my professional career as an investment banker, where I worked on M&A and capital restructuring mandates for banks and insurance companies in the US and Europe.
I did my MBA from IIM Lucknow and my undergraduate degree from SRCC, Delhi University. I’m also a CFA Charterholder.

rows.name: Abbie Lee
lines: I’m a Senior Client Service Associate at GC Wealth, based in Cambridge, MA.

At GC Wealth, I’m committed to delivering exceptional client experiences while overseeing operations and trading for my team. I excel at deepening relationships while managing the operational aspects of wealth management.

Before joining GC Wealth, I spent two years at First Republic Wealth Management, supporting clients in achieving their financial goals. I hold a degree in Business Management Studies from Gettysburg College and am currently pursuing an MBA at Babson College.
A fierce competitor, I’m also a decorated lacrosse player, having won two Division III Women’s Lacrosse National Championships.

rows.name: Adit Swarup
lines: I’m a Partner at General Catalyst where I’m building the Customer Value Fund. I work with founders that choose to create the largest possible versions of their businesses by co-investing in their growth every quarter throughout their journey to become enduring.

Prior to joining GC, I co-founded and led Rakuten’s venture capital arm, Rakuten Ventures. I was fortunate to find partnership and friendship in founders of many first-of-their kind software businesses that continue to lead the markets they created.
I’ve lived in 9 countries across 4 continents, and I’ve seen talent and ambition in every part of the world. Who we build with matters more than where we build.
I’m currently based in San Francisco.

rows.name: Ahmad Nasir
lines: I'm a first-generation American, and my parents taught me that being American is more than a privilege—it's a responsibility. I believe the opportunities this country provides come with a duty to serve our communities and our nation.

That belief led me to serve as a Green Beret in the U.S. Army for nearly a decade, including a deployment to Syria where my team's mission was to defeat ISIS. Serving in those environments taught me to work with a team under pressure, make decisions with imperfect information, and stay focused on the mission.

Those lessons continue to shape how I partner with founders today. At General Catalyst, I focus on the company’s Global Resilience strategy, partnering with founders building in AI, defense, energy, industrials, and other mission-critical technologies.

I earned a B.S. from the United States Military Academy, an M.Phil. from the University of Oxford, a J.D. from Stanford Law School, and an M.B.A. from the Stanford Graduate School of Business. Outside of my venture work, I continue to serve in the U.S. Army Reserve and volunteer with several veterans organizations and initiatives.

rows.name: Ajoy Prabakar
lines: In my role, I lead the Finance function for General Catalyst, India. My responsibilities include managing the India Advisor entity’s finance and taxation, overseeing all tax matters for GC vehicles investing into the country, and advising on transaction tax structuring and portfolio restructurings, I also manage financial due diligence for growth-stage companies, alongside handling end-to-end fund finance, valuations, and LP reporting for legacy Venture Highway funds.

Before joining GC, I led the finance function for a couple of private equity funds, including Venture Highway. I started my career in the EY Assurance team and worked at Citibank for about five years before transitioning into the private equity industry.
I am a Chartered Accountant and earned my executive MBA from XLRI Jamshedpur.
Outside of work, I love spending time playing with my young daughter. On Sundays, you can reliably find me on the cricket ground, happily braving the scorching Chennai heat.

rows.name: Akarsh Shrivastava
lines: I come to GC from Elevation Capital, where I most recently led the SaaS/AI and B2B practice and previously co-led the consumer tech practice. I was instrumental in rebooting and scaling the SaaS practice for the fund, from setting up the team to building the sourcing muscle and networks, and subsequently scaling the practice from less than 10% of the fund historically to around 30%.

Before Elevation, I spent three years at McKinsey & Company, where I worked across sectors and functions, including pharmaceuticals, financial services, and infrastructure, focusing on strategy, market launch, transformation projects, cost optimization, and product development.
I earned my bachelor's degree in civil engineering from the Indian Institute of Technology, Delhi, and my post-graduate diploma in management from the Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad.
I am interested in cricket, food, political history, and historical fiction, and I'm always happy to share suggestions for hidden food gems in Delhi.

rows.name: Alessandra Cesano
lines: I have been the Chief Medical Officer at ESSA Pharma since July 2019.

Previously, I was the Chief Medical Officer of NanoString Inc. from July 2015 to June 2019, where I focused on the development of translational and diagnostic multi-plexed assays for the characterization and measurement of immune response/resistance mechanisms.

Prior to joining NanoString, I served as the Chief Medical Officer at Cleave Biosciences, Inc., and before that, I was the Chief Medical Officer and Chief Operations Officer at Nodality, Inc. There, I built and led the R&D group while providing the overall clinical vision for the organization. Between 1998 and 2008, I held various management positions at Amgen, Biogen Idec, and SmithKline Beecham Pharmaceuticals, where I helped advance several oncology drugs through late-stage development and FDA approvals.
Early in my career, I spent 12 years researching tumor immunology, including nine years at the Wistar Institute, an NCI Basic Cancer Center affiliated with the University of Pennsylvania.

I am also a member of several professional and scientific societies, including ASCO, ESMO, ASH, EHA, AACR, and SITC. Within SITC, I co-chair the SITC Industry Committee, serve as an Associate Editor for the Biomarker section of JITC, and actively participate in the SITC Biomarker Working Group.
Throughout my career, I have authored over 140 publications.
I received my MD summa cum laude, a Board Certification in Oncology, and a PhD in Tumor Immunology from the University of Turin.
rows.title: Catalyst Advisor

rows.name: Alex Allaire
lines: I serve as the Analyst and Finance & Energy Policy Lead at the General Catalyst Institute (GCI) where I work to shape policy frameworks that support innovation across financial technology, digital assets, and energy infrastructure. This includes engaging with policymakers, regulators, and portfolio companies on the legislative and regulatory developments critical to scaling transformative technologies in the United States and abroad.

Prior to my current role, I served as a FinTech & Blockchain Policy Fellow in the U.S. House of Representatives under Majority Whip Tom Emmer, where I worked directly on emerging technology policy at the federal level. My time on the Hill provided firsthand exposure to the legislative process shaping crypto markets, decentralized finance, and financial innovation, collaborating with a broad set of stakeholders across Congress, federal agencies, and the private sector.

Earlier in my career, I served as an Industry Affairs Associate at the Blockchain Association, advancing the interests of the blockchain ecosystem and contributing to coalition-building around responsible digital asset regulation. I also co-founded the American Blockchain Initiative, helping to educate policymakers on blockchain technology and its policy implications during the industry's formative years in Washington.

I received my BA in Political Science with a concentration in American Government and reside in Washington, DC. When I'm not tracking legislation or policy developments, you can find me hiking, golfing, or spending time by the water.

rows.name: Alex Mackenzie
lines: I’m an investor at General Catalyst, a venture capital firm that partners with founders from seed through growth stages and beyond to build companies that withstand the test of time. At GC, I'm focused on driving our AI & Infra investing across Europe. As a software-engineer-turned-investor, you'll still find me picking up new tools/infra, building my own projects on weekends (currently building my own chess engine), and writing about the infra that I'm particularly excited about on my technical blog (mack.work).

Prior to joining GC I was an Investor at Tapestry VC in London, where I led many of our investments across AI, Infra and Cybersecurity, including in companies like: Tracebit, Maze, Keycard, Flox and Oleria. I was fortunate to start my career at VMware in Palo Alto, which is where I first learned about "VC" (not to mention ESXi and vSphere fundamentals, of course).

I graduated from Northeastern University (BS, International Business) & Dublin City University (BA, in Global Business) through a dual degree program. Boston is a wonderful city, particularly with an Irish accent.
Away from work, I like playing/watching rugby, electric guitar, anime, chess, bouldering, and just generally being humbled by picking up new things.

rows.name: Alex Tran
lines: I grew up in Silicon Valley and studied at Stanford, where I was surrounded by intellectually curious people who were constantly questioning and challenging the status quo. This is why I love talking to entrepreneurs who can pick apart industries, question the way things are, and dream how things should and might be.

I started in venture capital in 2012, when I joined the growth-stage investing team at Kleiner Perkins. That was 5 years after the iPhone was released and mobile internet adoption was accelerating. Every platform shift leads to an explosion in new companies, and I feel very fortunate to have had a front row seat to some truly iconic businesses of that era. I also helped chronicle a lot of this development in the Internet Trends reports we published. Today, we are in the middle of another technology platform shift with artificial intelligence (AI), and I'm incredibly excited to back founders solving problems with AI.

In 2017, I took a year off to travel around the world. My learning accelerates when I go somewhere new, because it forces me to think from first principles: how does one country’s experience differ from another, how did that come to be, and if we could reimagine it with a blank slate, how would we build it?  The pockets of leapfrogging that happen can give us a glimpse into the future. I love paying attention to the myriad of new internet users who are coming online all around the world: they bring with them cultural nuances and consumer behaviors that lead to beautiful and unique products.

At General Catalyst, I lead our growth investing practice as well as our fintech and consumer sectors. I invest globally and work closely with Ramp, Aven, and Thatch in the US, Monzo in the UK, and CRED in India, just to name a few. Outside of work, I enjoy cycling, playing board games, reading, and occasionally wandering a little too far from home.
rows.title: Managing Director

rows.name: Alexa Liautaud
lines: Shaped by my roots in Europe and the United States, I developed an early fascination with how different systems, technologies, and people quietly define outcomes. I believe entrepreneurship remains one of the most powerful mechanisms for real, lasting change.

At General Catalyst, I partner closely with extraordinary founders from the very earliest stages onward, committing across our generalist platform. My focus spans applied AI, software, and hardware. That also includes our Global Resilience thesis, working with founders taking on seemingly impossible yet critical missions, among them Anduril, Castelion, Nominal, Senra, Chariot and several in stealth.

I found my way into venture capital by way of journalism. Reporting at Bloomberg, the Wall Street Journal, and NBC News, allowed me to explore the world, ask questions, and connect with people of all backgrounds. Prior, I received my B.A. in History and an MBA from Stanford University, and an M.S. in journalism from Columbia Journalism School.

rows.name: Alexandre Momeni
lines: Growing up as an Iranian immigrant made me aware early on that access to opportunity, security, and technology was not evenly distributed. I began my career at Goldman Sachs, drawn to the role capital plays in shaping global economies and societies, but quickly became convinced that entrepreneurs building at the frontier would be an even more powerful force for change.

At General Catalyst, I partner with founders globally from the earliest stages through growth and beyond, with a focus on frontier intelligence, robotics, and science. I’m especially interested in moments when technological advances make entirely new products and businesses possible in critical industries. This includes working with founders pursuing difficult, consequential problems, such as AIRE, Black Forest Labs, Chai Discovery, Mistral AI, Hippocratic AI, amongst others.

Before joining GC, I spent a few years on the trading floor at Goldman Sachs, conducted AI research at Stanford, and built products at Nabla, learning to see the world through different questions and from different vantage points. Prior to that, I received a BS in Economics from the London School of Economics, an MS in Mathematics from École polytechnique, and an MS in Management from HEC Paris.

rows.name: Ali Jordan
lines: As Head of Strategic Relationships at General Catalyst, I focus on building the connective tissue that helps our Famiglia do its best work together.

Before joining GC, I spent over a decade at Innovation Endeavors working closely with founders at the intersection of advanced technology and real-world industries. As an operating partner, I headed up founder success, with roles spanning value creation, marketing and communications, investor relations, and operations. I loved building programs that brought people together in unexpected ways including Curiosity Camp, an off-the-grid gathering that grew into a flagship event for scientists, technologists, artists, and business leaders. Earlier in my career, I worked in fashion PR and communications at brands like Jimmy Choo and Diane von Furstenberg, where I helped build the connections that brought their worlds to life.
I have a B.A. in English Literature from UCLA. I live in Menlo Park with my husband Brett and my two kids, Bodie and Charlie.

rows.name: Amanda Velluto
lines: I’ve spent my career making compliance a front-end platform for success rather than a back-end review after the work is done. I win converts with my engaging powers of communication and collaboration, combined with deep experience in how rules and regulations continuously evolve alongside innovations in finance and investing.

At General Catalyst, I support the firm’s growth while addressing the desire in society and among investors for greater transparency in how capital and the economy intersect. I’ve observed that venture capital now comes from a broader range of investors with varied levels of experience and sophistication – yet they all deserve the same assurance that their needs and goals are in good hands.

As a veteran of successful, team-focused financial firms, I’ve collaborated closely with legal and operations experts across core activities, from prospecting to reporting. One hallmark of my work is ensuring that operating policies are tailored to the organization and how it works, so that compliance is built in and breakthrough achievements always take place within the proper bounds.

Outside the office, I’m a regular on the tennis court and on the sidelines of lacrosse fields where my children play. I’m also a long-time volunteer with groups benefiting women and children, and I support the Boston Athletic Association, the organizers of the world-famous Boston Marathon.

rows.name: Amrita Mainthia
lines: I am always asking questions because questions lead to answers that inform a way forward. What do our founders need? Our limited partners? Our society? I am driven to meet these needs with the same level of innovation that our entrepreneurs bring to their own companies.

One of the formative professional experiences in my career was working on GE’s divestment of GE Capital. The size and complexity of the transactions, the number of stakeholders involved, and the communications challenges were massive, but what impressed me most were the leaders who maintained their integrity and authenticity throughout, with everyone from investors to employees to regulators. My experience there inspired me to continue building the skills I would need to become that type of leader.

At General Catalyst, I have the opportunity to support our investment team and portfolio companies in their quest to reshape markets and industries. Using my experience in journalism and communications, I test business strategies by shaping the stories around them. Stories are how we communicate what matters to us, and the right story about a strategy can influence how we make decisions and develop our business. Done well, stories inspire others to join in our mission. Every successful founder knows this from experience, and I love bringing this perspective to our fundraising efforts and relationships.

Outside the office, I spend time mentoring college seniors as part of my alumni involvement with Syracuse University. You can often find me trying new recipes, reading long-form thought pieces, and slowly reacquainting myself with life as a California resident.

rows.name: Anant Pai
lines: I am an investor on the Health Assurance team, partnering with founders from the earliest to growth stages and beyond.

After considering a career in international development (working at the World Bank and non-profits in Latin America and the Caribbean), I began my career at McKinsey & Company, where I focused on performing commercial due diligence and partnering with large organizations (healthcare providers, governments, and foundations) on digital transformation. Prior to General Catalyst, I worked as an investor at Revolution, a multi-stage venture capital firm where I focused on early stage investments across sectors, including fintech, enterprise software, and healthcare.

Coming from a family of healthcare practitioners, I am excited about GC’s focus on systems-level transformation that tackles the expansive set of operational, clinical, technological, and social challenges that can cause illness. I hope to partner with visionary founders who have intimate knowledge of these challenges and support them in realizing solutions that preventatively care for patients, align incentives across parties, and contain rising healthcare costs.

I hold a BA in Applied Mathematics from Harvard College. Outside of work, you can catch me hosting dinner parties and trying out new recipes, sampling workout classes, voraciously consuming audio books and podcasts (but somehow always managing to add content to my list more quickly than I can consume it), or binge-watching reality TV (which I will deny vehemently).

rows.name: Anastasia Borukhov
lines: I joined GC Wealth's San Francisco office as a Director of Compliance to help manage various aspects of the expanding and increasingly complex wealth compliance program.

Prior to joining GC Wealth, I spent almost 20 years in the financial industry. Starting out as a financial representative and financial analyst, I found my compliance calling after joining Partners Group, a Swiss-based private equity firm. Since then, I have honed my compliance skills by working at various hedge funds, including Partners Fund Management (PFM) and Jackson Square Partners, LLC, and by joining the consulting firm Constellation Advisers, LLC, where I continued to gain deep compliance expertise. Before joining GC Wealth, I spent a few years as a Vice President at the turnkey asset management platform, Freedom Investment Management.

I hold a BS in Economics and Business Administration from Saint Mary's College in Moraga, CA. Outside of my professional life, I enjoy reading, hosting family and friends, skiing, and canyoneering with the members of our book club, as well as spending time with my husband, two kids, and our German Shepherd pup.

rows.name: Andrew Burge
lines: As Chief Administrative Officer for GC Wealth, I lead the finance, business strategy and risk management functions for our business. My focus is on supporting our team to serve the founders, entrepreneurs, and families in our General Catalyst community with excellence and intention.

Before joining GC Wealth, I served as Managing Director and Chief Financial Officer for J.P. Morgan Advisors, leading the Finance and Business Management Team supporting the division’s 600 financial advisors and $330 billion in client assets. Prior to that I spent over fifteen years at First Republic Bank, ultimately serving as Chief Administrative Officer for First Republic Private Wealth Management.

Each of these experiences reinforced my belief that the best businesses are built on a foundation of disciplined execution, strategic clarity, and genuine care for the people we get to work with and serve.
I joined GC Wealth because I believe in the power of aligning an entrepreneurial mindset with operational rigor and putting relationships at the center of everything we do.
I earned my B.A. from the University of Southern California and live in the San Francisco Bay Area with my wife and daughter.
rows.title: Chief Administrative Officer, GC Wealth

rows.name: Anna Geor
lines: My experience in the finance industry is largely within operations, leading large teams of people whose performance had a material impact on the company’s brand and customer satisfaction. Eventually, I began looking at things in the opposite direction to understand how the company was affecting the performance of its people. That led me into HR, where I could help develop corporate culture and business policies from a more holistic perspective that meets the needs of both the enterprise and its people.

One of the main lessons of that experience is that people want to do business with people, almost regardless of technology, brand, or other factors. This is even more true in the investment world, where capital and technology go hand-in-hand. The human factor becomes even more important, not less. That’s why I jumped at the chance to join General Catalyst and become part of an organization that has prioritized sustaining the culture that has made it so successful.

I grew up in New Zealand and still go home to visit family when I can. I also look around to see where I can help out in the community, including the Red Cross. I now reside in New York, where I am able to spend time enjoying the arts, interior design, good food, and getting outdoors in nature.

rows.name: Boomer Dell
lines: There are quite a few engineers in my family, going back generations, and I think that influences why I look at language as a form of architecture and as a living structure. I experienced law school through that lens: law as language engineered to design, build, and hopefully improve interactions and relationships of all kinds.

As a regulatory compliance officer, lawyer, and risk manager, I know certain measures of success are quantitative; however, all success in these endeavors stems from language and communication. The more effectively and positively one connects with others, the better the results, whether pitching a start-up idea or building consensus on a complex policy matter.

Before joining General Catalyst, I worked for Fidelity, Russell Investments, and Ares Management, all of which provided incredible learning and growth opportunities during notable change. Markets, products, services, and regulatory environments worldwide evolve constantly, requiring a high level of sophistication. I continuously educate myself in myriad ways to keep pace with the leading edges of law, finance, and technology.

This perspective is what brought me to General Catalyst. Compliance is not just a fancy word for “don’t break the rules”; it is about enhancing enterprise value to attract the most promising investment opportunities, investors, strategic partners, and people.

I graduated with a BA from Boston College, a JD from Suffolk University Law School, an LLM from BU School of Law, and I earned two Certificates, one in fintech and one in applied AI, from MIT. Outside of work, I am happily devoted to family. My wife and I love to travel and explore with our teens and spend time with our extended “clan” of family and friends. I am a music student at Berklee College of Music’s online program, and I pursue art in various ways to keep the layers of my mind engaged and happy. As a family, we support charitable organizations devoted to helping people in specific ways that have affected our lives personally.
rows.title: Chief Compliance Officer

rows.name: Arielle Gross Samuels
lines: As Chief Marketing & Communications Officer at General Catalyst, I lead a global team focused on brand, marketing, press, marketing technology, thought leadership, and experiential marketing to support our company and portfolio. I’m passionate about unlocking growth for entrepreneurs, and believe that anyone should be able to turn a good idea into a great opportunity. Working at General Catalyst allows me to play to that passion every day.

My background before GC spans finance at Blackstone where I was the firm’s Global Head of Marketing, nearly a decade at Meta (fka Facebook) where I founded global teams in Product Development and Business Marketing, and Engineering Consulting at Deloitte.
For years, I’ve done board and coalition work with the United Nations Foundation’s Girl Up, Geena Davis Institute, University of Illinois Alumni Association, 92NY and as a founding member of Chief.
My degree is in Materials Science and Engineering from the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, where I endowed the Engineering Visionary Scholarship to support inclusion in STEM.
rows.title: Chief Marketing & Communications Officer

rows.name: Arif Ahmed
lines: As an Executive Vice President of GC Wealth at General Catalyst, I am dedicated to leading and growing our client franchise. I partner closely with GC's leadership and the entire GC team to serve the comprehensive financial and family office needs of our Famiglia. My core focus is on building durable, long-term relationships that compound both trust and performance over time.

Before joining General Catalyst, I spent over 25 years in wealth management at institutions including J.P. Morgan, First Republic Bank, and Merrill Lynch. At First Republic, I was instrumental in scaling the private wealth division, building a service model centered on bespoke advice and exceptional responsiveness. This work deepened my expertise across complex balance sheets, multigenerational planning, and delivering institutional-grade solutions for families and founders.

I began my career at Merrill Lynch in 1998, which laid the foundation for working with venture capitalists, founders, executives, and early employees of some of the world's most influential technology companies.
rows.title: EVP, Head of Family Office

rows.name: Ashley Paston
lines: Born into a family with strong entrepreneurial roots, I witnessed early on the power of compounding dedication and resilience. I attended Wharton Business School at the University of Pennsylvania, where I received a Bachelor of Science in Finance. I began my career at McKinsey in their Strategy & Corporate Finance group, where I gained early exposure to some of the best companies across the globe. It was there that I was able to codify the underpinnings of what drives generational companies. I then spent the better part of the last decade at venture firms - first at Bain Capital Ventures and then at Meritech.

I joined General Catalyst as a Partner excited to back the next generation of enterprise software companies. I am excited to work with founders who approach the world with a strong sense of curiosity, peeling back the layers of markets and having the tenacity to shape the world in accordance with their vision. Outside of work, I love any form of live entertainment (concerts, art exhibits, stand up, musicals), board games, wandering through new neighborhoods, and testing out my pain threshold while rooting for the NY Jets.

rows.name: Athul Jacob
lines: I am the Co-founder and Chief AI Officer at Percepta (a GC Transformation Company) where I help critical industries accelerate their transformation with frontier AI and decision-making.
Based in Cambridge, I also collaborate closely with GC’s Creation team on hatch and buyout initiatives centered on AI, and partner with investment teams across Ignition and Endurance.

Before Percepta, I worked on AI agents and strategic decision-making at Google, Meta, and Microsoft, and served as a GC AI Fellow. I hold a bachelor’s degree in computer science, combinatorics, and optimization from the University of Waterloo and a Ph.D. in AI from MIT.
I split time between Cambridge, New York, and San Francisco as we build Percepta’s capabilities and support GC companies on their AI journeys.
rows.title: Co-founder & Chief AI Officer, Percepta

rows.name: Ben Huang
lines: I’m a senior analyst at GC Wealth, a next-generation wealth management platform built for transformational individuals, families, and organizations, and a critical component of GC’s effort to go Beyond Venture. At GC Wealth, I focus on portfolio management and research. I’m based in Bellevue, Washington.
I joined GC Wealth after a decade of experience with major banks in the U.S. and Canada, most recently at First Republic Bank, where I served clients’ investment needs.
Outside of work, I enjoy traveling, exploring culinary delights with my wife Jenny, and spending quality time with our beloved Pomeranian BoBo. I’ve recently picked up pet photography as a new hobby.

rows.name: Bill Fitzgerald
lines: As a co-founder, former Chief Operating Officer and Managing Director, I played a key role in major decisions spanning finance, legal, operations, fundraising, and portfolio management, as well as business expansion strategy and execution. In March of 2020, I transitioned to the role of Strategic Advisor. One of our strongest values as a firm is the commitment we have to collaborate with and challenge each other. That goes back years before we founded General Catalyst, when a number of us worked together at various companies, ranging from startups to national industry leaders. Today we listen to and mentor our entrepreneurs to take the same approach: build a team based on open, honest communication about roles, responsibilities, risks, and rewards. This approach has enabled us to seek out different opinions and embrace ambiguity. Many of our best investments were highly debated decisions at the time, and we were able to have the right conversations and make the right call.

Before co-founding General Catalyst, I co-founded and operated a number of businesses with Joel Cutler and David Fialkow in the travel, information services, specialty retail, consumer direct marketing and payment processing industries. Prior to that, I was vice president and treasurer of a private equity group that acquired under-performing or strategically challenged businesses. Prior to that, I was a manager with KPMG and an adjunct professor at Boston College. I graduated with a B.A. from the College Of The Holy Cross, and received a J.D. from Suffolk University Law School. I am a current or former member of the Massachusetts Bar and Certified Public Accountants Associations, the Association for Corporate Growth, the Financial Executives Institute and Director of the Private Equity CFO Association. I am an avid sports fan and believe there is no substitute for sacrifice, preparation, teamwork and sportsmanship.

rows.name: Bill Grinnell
lines: I am a Wealth Manager at GC Wealth, a next-generation wealth management platform built for transformational individuals, families, and organizations and a critical component of GC’s endeavor to go Beyond Venture. I am based in Cambridge, MA.
At GC Wealth, I leverage 30+ years of experience to foster deep, enduring relationships with clients, many of which span multiple generations.

I began my career as a municipal bond portfolio manager at Goldman Sachs Asset Management in NYC in 1985. Prior to joining GC Wealth, I was a Managing Director at First Republic and founding partner of the Private Wealth Management Team.

Outside of work, I am dedicated to education and have served on boards of The Pingree School and The Tower School. I am also a passionate advocate for the LGBTQI community. In my free time, I enjoy open water swimming and have successfully escaped from Alcatraz!

rows.name: Biz Peabody
lines: I am an Operating Partner at General Catalyst for the Global Resilience portfolio. I partner with founders building in defense, industrial, energy and beyond — helping them navigate the operational and strategic challenges that are unique to mission-driven companies at scale.

Prior to General Catalyst, I spent six years at Shield AI, where I helped grow the company from a $200 million Series B startup to a $12.7 billion defense technology leader. I served as Chief of Staff and led Investor Relations while building business models, processes, and entire functions from scratch — going wherever the company needed me most. Before that, I was a contract negotiator for Raytheon's multi-billion-dollar radar portfolio, which gave me early fluency in defense acquisition from the prime contractor lens.

At GC, I work alongside portfolio founders on the challenging operational problems that come with scaling a resilient company, including navigating government acquisition, designing lasting business models, scaling manufacturing processes, preparing for institutional capital, communicating the mission, and building the teams and functions that make growth sustainable.

I grew up in a family that believes deeply in service, and the many forms it can take. I've found my life's passion in building and enabling the companies at the center of our national security and resilience. There is no mission I'd rather be close to.
I'm a Certified Federal Contracts Manager. I hold a BA in International Relations from USC, an MBA from Harvard Business School, and an MPP from Harvard Kennedy School.
rows.title: Operating Partner

rows.name: Bob Thornton
lines: As CEO of GC Wealth, I lead the company’s wealth platform built for transformational individuals, families, and organizations.  GC Wealth oversees the investment and research activities to be introduced for the benefit of our wealth management clients and other members of the GC community.

I joined GC in 2025 following 18 years leading First Republic Private Wealth Management, one of the nation’s largest wealth management businesses.  Before that, I was a Managing Director at Deutsche Bank, where I led the firm’s technology mergers & acquisition practice, a role I previously held at Lehman Brothers.

I began my professional career at Goldman Sachs, where I was a member of both the Corporate Finance and Mergers & Acquisitions departments.  Subsequently, I served as Head of West Coast Mergers & Acquisitions at Credit Suisse.

I graduated with a B.A. degree from Duke University and then a J.D. degree from the Columbia University School of Law.  I also served as a clerk for Judge Carolyn Dineen Randall of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit.
rows.title: CEO, GC Wealth

rows.name: Brad Rose
lines: I am the Head of Healthcare Partnerships and Growth at HATCo, the healthcare transformation arm of global investment and transformation company General Catalyst. I serve as the primary leader for HATCo's strategic partnering efforts, building relationships with their 23 Health Assurance partners and guiding growth strategy as the organization matures its transformation services capabilities. I work closely with GC portfolio companies and founders to understand their capabilities and advise on refining solutions that align with healthcare transformation objectives.

I bring extensive experience in healthcare transformation. Most recently, I was the founder and CEO of BDR Advisory Services, where I led strategy, growth, and advisory support for healthcare, investment, and services companies. Prior to that, I spent over a decade at The Advisory Board Company, collaborating with numerous multi-billion-dollar health system clients to drive strategic initiatives and operational improvements.

Through my role at HATCo, I am committed to advancing the mission of transforming healthcare delivery across high-value enterprise relationships, working to build a more resilient and proactive healthcare system that prioritizes keeping people well while making quality care more affordable and accessible.
I hold a bachelor's degree in political science and government from Emory University.

rows.name: Brian Carew
lines: I’m an analyst at GC Wealth, where I support client relationships, manage performance reporting, and conduct investment research. I’m based in Jackson, WY.
Before joining GC Wealth, I held banking positions at First Republic and Wells Fargo, where I served clients’ various banking needs and built relationships in the Jackson community for over a decade.
I graduated from Sewanee: The University of the South with a BA in Economics. Away from GC, you’ll find me volunteering as a ski instructor with Coombs Club, fishing, or golfing.

rows.name: Brian Leman
lines: I am an Analyst at GC Wealth based in San Francisco, where I am responsible for creating detailed portfolio reports, conducting in-depth performance analysis, and tracking private investments to provide insights for the team.

Prior to joining GC Wealth, I worked in Wealth Management at J.P. Morgan and First Republic Bank. I hold a B.S. in Applied Mathematics from the University of California, San Diego. Outside of work, I enjoy watching sports and movies, and am an avid fan of FC Barcelona and Messi.

rows.name: Caitlin Donovan
lines: I’m a highly recognized builder and operator in the healthcare space, and I share a commitment to making health assurance a reality—where healthcare is more accessible, proactive, and affordable for all.

Most recently, I was the Global Head of Uber Health, Uber’s business unit focused on creating a first-of-its-kind supplemental benefit platform offering non-emergency transportation, prescription delivery, grocery, and over-the-counter item benefits to Medicare Advantage, Managed Medicaid, and Commercial populations. During my 3-year tenure there, I substantially scaled the business, reimagining how technology intersects with healthcare.

Before Uber Health, I served as Chief Operating Officer and VP of Operations in various businesses focused on medical transportation, home health, multi-clinic providers, and post-acute care. Early in my career, I worked as an investor at Bain Capital and Summit Partners, where I built a strong understanding of finance.
I earned my bachelor’s degree in Economics from Harvard University, and I live in Dover, Massachusetts, with my husband and two boys.

rows.name: Candace Richardson
lines: I grew up in Asheville, North Carolina watching the news every night believing I would become a journalist, keen to have a grasp on what was happening around the world and why. After moving to NYC for college I continued on this pursuit academically, studying economics, philosophy and history but my career aspirations evolved, and like many at that age I entered an exploratory phase professionally. After discovering that my mother had been a political activist in Ethiopia before she emigrated, I traveled there with her to create an oral history project on the role of secondary students in the Ethiopian Revolution, and that got me thinking about a career in academia. I also spent time at a think tank to explore economic policy at the federal and state level. In the end, I received and followed wise advice that a career in finance would keep me connected to current events, and the integral role capital markets play in shaping them, while affording me the opportunity to make a difference in the world.

Beginning my career at Goldman Sachs, I got a fast, immersive education in healthcare finance across the capital structure. I furthered my interest at Town Hall Ventures, where I was able to work closely with companies that serve medically vulnerable and historically underserved patient populations. And because the firm was relatively small, I was able to contribute across a range of essential activities, from raising a fund and portfolio management to observing boards.

General Catalyst has a tremendous opportunity and influence in healthcare, including how care is delivered and paid for successfully, and equitably, for all stakeholders. The firm also has deep technology and consumer experience that is essential to the transformation of healthcare from a “sick care” system to a more proactive and resilient Health Assurance system designed to make quality care more affordable and accessible to help people stay well.

It’s probably no surprise that I enjoy tackling big problems that require extensive collaboration to dissolve barriers and create new solutions. I think of it as a combination of lofty and grounded, creative and practical. It’s the same in my personal life, where you can find me painting one day and teaching tennis to kids the next.

rows.name: Carin Watson
lines: I’m Chief of Staff to Hemant Taneja at General Catalyst, based in GC’s San Francisco office.

Before joining GC, I was the Chief Growth Officer at Singularity University. Previously, I served as the Executive Vice President of Learning & Innovation and Managing Director of Corporate Innovation at Singularity University. Earlier in my career, I was the Director of Innovation in the Citi Ventures division at Citigroup, Inc.
I received my MBA from The Kellogg School of Management at Northwestern University and a BS in Management Science from the University of California, San Diego.

rows.name: Charlotte Rock
lines: I am the Vice President of Public Policy for Healthcare at the General Catalyst Institute. I've always been fascinated by the intersection of healthcare and technology, and particularly by how policy can either enable or inhibit innovation that improves people's lives.

I grew up in Atlanta, Georgia, and studied Public Policy at Georgia Tech. After college, I spent more than eight years in the United States Senate, where policy became much more than theory for me. I held key health policy roles with Senator David Perdue (now U.S. Ambassador to China), on the Senate Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions (HELP) Committee, and the Senate Finance Committee, where I led the Medicaid portfolio overseeing reforms for the program that serves over 70 million Americans. I saw firsthand how the rules we write shape what's possible in healthcare.

What drew me from the Senate to the General Catalyst Institute was the opportunity to work at the front lines of healthcare innovation: to help shape policies that don't just react to technology but actively enable it to reach the people who need it most. At GCI, I lead healthcare policy initiatives and coordinate federal engagement for GC's health assurance investment portfolio. I work closely with Congress and federal agencies including HHS, CMS, FDA, and ARPA-H to advance policy priorities and support portfolio companies as they navigate federal opportunities and regulatory requirements.
My mom is French, so I grew up speaking fluent French and developed a love for traveling and cooking. I'm based in Washington, DC, where I live with my husband, Stuart.

rows.name: Charmel Maynard
lines: I sit on John Utendahl's Impact Initiatives team.

Prior to GC, I served as the Chief Investment Officer & Treasurer for the University of Miami where I led UM's efforts to invest over $4B in assets, including endowment and pension funds. I was also responsible for the University's $2B capital structure, including liquidity and debt issuances. Additionally, I managed treasury and cash management.

I was previously a vice president with J.P. Morgan's Investment Bank in New York City. During my 10-year career with J.P. Morgan, I focused on investment banking, debt capital markets and leveraged finance, where I advised clients on capital structure solutions, deal structuring, and execution of syndicated revolving credit facilities, institutional term loans, and bond issuances.
I hold a Bachelor of Arts in political science from Amherst College.
rows.title: Managing Director

rows.name: Chelsea Toledo
lines: I’m a Senior Client Service Associate at GC Wealth, where I focus on day-to-day client requests, trades, strategy implementation, data analysis, and maintenance. I’m based in Jackson, Wyoming.
Before joining GC Wealth, I worked as a client service associate for 4 years at First Republic Private Wealth Management, and later at JP Morgan Wealth Management.
I graduated from Colorado Mesa University with a BA in Science and also hold a certificate in AI (Artificial Intelligence) and Machine Learning from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.
When I’m not working in wealth management, you can find me fly fishing for trout on the Snake River, snowboarding in the Tetons, or cycling the gravel trails around Jackson.

rows.name: Chloe Hemingway
lines: I am a Talent Partner at General Catalyst, leading Executive Talent for our Global Resilience practice. I partner with visionary founders building companies that are transforming critical sectors such as defense, intelligence, industrials, energy, and climate. My work centers on cultivating a world-class talent network and advising on strategic executive hiring to drive business success, build talent-dense organizations, and navigate every stage of scale. Based in Los Angeles, I am passionate about companies driving paradigm shifts and believe talent is one of the most powerful levers for achieving long-term growth.

Prior to joining General Catalyst, I was the first Head of Talent at True Anomaly, an aerospace and defense startup, where I built and led the talent function from Seed to Series C. I oversaw all executive, technical, and non-technical hiring as the company grew 4× in two years, expanded from Denver into Los Angeles, and established a data-driven recruiting function. I scaled the internal talent team from one to seven, implemented systems and processes to support rapid growth, and led critical hiring across the business. Earlier in my career, I spent five years in executive search at Daversa Partners, where I launched and grew the firm’s frontier technology practice in Los Angeles, executing searches for leading startups and industry pioneers across hardware and software.

I graduated from UCLA with a BA in Psychology and Communications, where I was also a four-year member of the Division I women’s soccer team. Athletics shaped my perspective on leadership, psychological safety, and the value of authentic relationships in driving team success. Outside of work, I enjoy yoga, fitness, exploring new restaurants, and spending time at the beach. I believe connection is the foundation of everything I do, both in my work and in my life.

rows.name: Chris Bischoff
lines: I started my career in management consulting, where I helped clients develop new strategies to adapt to evolving market needs. After business school, I gravitated to investment banking, where I advised technology, media, and telecoms companies on structuring, financing, and executing transformational transactions.

I found my calling in investing in early-stage companies as it offers the challenge and reward of partnering with talented founders to build new and better businesses faster. As an investor, I have focused on addressing material, everyday needs with innovative data-driven products and services. I am motivated by tackling challenges that matter, and by leveraging technology to create positive, enduring change.

Not surprisingly this approach led me to spend time in healthcare, where every interaction involves important choices, costs, and outcomes, and the system needs to become more sustainable - affordable, accessible, equitable, empathetic, and effective. It also led me to initially partner with and then join General Catalyst. I experienced first hand the firm’s maker mentality at Livongo and the desire to serve those most in need at Cityblock. The General Catalyst ethos of responsible innovation and radical collaboration is critical in healthcare, where entrepreneurs and traditional players need to work together to reinvent a better future.

Two of the most important themes of the next decade will be the transformation of healthcare and the development of Europe into a vibrant, technologically-driven economy across multiple sectors. I get excited by bringing to bear the amazing General Catalyst platform to support entrepreneurs in these two areas.

Whilst European, I consider myself a citizen of the world: I was born in Hong Kong, my parents are German and English, my wife is French and I have worked in the U.K., Europe, the U.S. and South East Asia. This is lucky as I work across multiple time zones and countries each day.

When not working with entrepreneurs, I love to travel, read and play competitive tennis. My family is actively involved in promoting ambitious environmental change and opening up higher education opportunities to students in lower income countries.
rows.title: COO GC Capital & Managing Director

rows.name: Chris McCain
lines: My official role is Chief Legal Officer, but at General Catalyst we all contribute to helping entrepreneurs overcome challenges, navigate obstacles, find creative solutions and seize opportunities.

As an undergraduate at Boston College, I knew early on that I wanted to be an attorney so I spent a year studying law at Oxford University. While at Boston College law school, I became interested in working with early-stage companies because I was inspired by young entrepreneurs and their ability to see opportunity when most others do not. My first job was with Gunderson Dettmer Stough Villeneuve Franklin & Hachigian, LLP, which has a strong venture capital practice. Working in one of the firm’s smaller offices, I was able to roll up my sleeves and quickly learn about the world of venture capital transactions, start-up company needs and growing pains, M&A, fund formation and public offerings.

After they opened their Boston office, I moved to Cooley LLP to benefit from their larger platform for supporting entrepreneurs, venture capital firms and complex M&A. Both Gunderson’s and Cooley’s roots are on the west coast, so I was able to have a window into the Silicon Valley approach to entrepreneurs and start-ups while also working here on the east coast.

Today, I seek to leverage these prior experiences to support our team of dynamic, creative and intelligent individuals here at General Catalyst as well as our diverse ecosystem of exceptional and talented entrepreneurs.

My wife and I have three young sons, who are the only people I know that have more energy than our entrepreneurs. When there’s time to relax (and there isn’t much with the boys), I enjoy throwing my support behind Boston’s sports teams (and, of course, the Boston College Eagles).
rows.title: Chief Legal Officer

rows.name: Chris Wolfe
lines: I am the Chief Investment Officer for GC Wealth, where I focus on identifying high-conviction themes across public and private markets to serve the founders, entrepreneurs, and families across the GC Famiglia. I work to develop tactical allocation views and source opportunities that align with our endurance mindset, helping our clients navigate the complexities of long-term wealth creation.

My career has been a series of chapters in rigor and resilience. I spent over thirty-five years in private wealth management, including as the Chief Investment Officer at First Republic Private Wealth Management, where I built the research and investment platform that became the backbone of the firm’s advisory experience. Prior to that, I led the Chief Investment Office for ultra-high-net-worth clients at Merrill Lynch and served as the Global Head of Equities for the JPMorgan Private Bank. Each of these roles taught me that the best investment thinking doesn't come from having all the answers, but from the humility to ask better questions.

I joined GC Wealth because I believe in the power of radical collaboration and putting the client relationship ahead of everything else. I earned my BS from the University of Rhode Island and my MBA from Columbia Business School, and I hold both the Certified Financial Planner and Chartered Financial Analyst designations.

Outside of work, I am guided by a lesson my mother taught me: that we always make time for what is important. For me, that means prioritizing presence and lifelong learning. I enjoy spending time with my family, staying curious about emerging market shifts, and ensuring I’m showing up prepared for the people counting on me.
rows.title: Chief Investment Officer, GC Wealth

rows.name: Christine Vasquez
lines: I’m a Senior Client Service Associate at GC Wealth. I bring a decade of experience serving high-net-worth clients’ business, lending, and investment needs.
At GC Wealth, I focus on the onboarding experience and process for the Wyoming team’s clientele, along with their cash management needs.

Outside of the office, I enjoy spending time with my husband, Delrick, and our dog Jyn. My hobbies include creating 3-D prints and traveling. In my free time, I also volunteer teaching financial literacy to underserved communities in Los Angeles.

rows.name: Christopher Kauffman
lines: I’m a Partner at General Catalyst, a venture capital firm that partners with founders from seed through growth stages and beyond to build companies that withstand the test of time. At GC, I focus on investments in later-stage enterprise and AI companies and partner with founders to build AI transformation platforms through our Creation strategy. I’m based in San Francisco.

Before joining GC, I was the Vice President of Finance at Ruggable LLC, where I focused on e-commerce. Prior to that, I was a Vice President in the Frontier Technologies sector at SoftBank Investment Advisers (SoftBank Vision Fund) and an Associate at Golden Gate Capital.

I received my BSc in Business, with a focus on finance and psychology, from Indiana University’s Kelley School of Business. Outside of the office, I can be found outdoors—either cycling or mountaineering—and in the local music scene. As a former drummer and bassist, I also actively support local musicians in advancing their careers.

rows.name: Clara Koster
lines: At GC, I focus on Portfolio Operations for the European portfolio, empowering founders with the extensive resources of a global platform and driving a comprehensive, value-focused approach to portfolio management.

Prior to joining GC, I led Platform and Portfolio Support at Cavalry Ventures, a Berlin-based early-stage fund, where I managed stakeholder relations, supported go-to-market strategies, and helped founders navigate fundraising and scaling. Before that, I spent over three years doing an M&A rollup in healthcare, leading acquisitions, due diligence, and post-merger integration. I am also the initiator of a community of VC platform professionals and operators in the DACH region, fostering collaboration and co-development for best-in-class portfolio and founder support.

I hold a Master’s degree in International Management from ESADE Business School in Barcelona and a Bachelor’s degree in Management and Technology from the Technical University of Munich, with a minor in Chemistry.
Outside of work, I’m passionate about cycling, yoga, art and food. I also enjoy singing and rapping—hidden "talents" that occasionally make an appearance.

rows.name: Courtney Celona
lines: My journey to General Catalyst was, in a literal sense, academic. After graduating, I taught history at the secondary level for a couple of years. What I loved most about teaching was the opportunity to engage with students daily, building rapport in the classroom, and fostering student engagement through the learning process. I admired their insatiable curiosities and desire to take their learnings from our lessons and channel them to help shape the future.

When I first met the team at GC, what drew me in was the mission, values, and energy of the firm. Although it was initially hard to imagine leaving the classroom, in many ways I embraced a learning mindset and was eager and energized to build my career with GC.

Fast forward to today, I’ve now spent nearly a decade with the firm in a number of roles, first across the administrative, finance, and operations functions, before ultimately choosing Client Solutions & Services, a role I’ve now had for the majority of my GC career.
My focus today is to ensure that all the needs of our limited partners are met with transparency, consistency, and the level of engagement we at GC know they deserve.

As someone who thrives on understanding the needs of and communicating with investors, I seek to cultivate meaningful, longstanding relationships, built off of transparency and trust. GC’s values, particularly Depth of Relationship, is a guiding principle in my career.

In my spare time I can be found down the Cape with my family, connecting with friends, or attending a group fitness class. I am a longtime resident of Boston and enjoy exploring the city in search of the best food and beverage in town. In fact, I enjoy doing that in any city I’m in, as traveling is a major passion as well!

rows.name: Daisy Zhao
lines: I'm on the seed team at General Catalyst, focused on backing exceptional founders at the very beginning. Most of my time is spent working with founders building in AI across applications and infrastructure.

Both of my parents are entrepreneurs, so I grew up with a firsthand appreciation for what it takes to build something from scratch. That upbringing gave me both a deep passion for the craft and genuine empathy for the founders who are in the thick of it. Before joining GC, I was on the early stage team at Andreessen Horowitz. Prior to a16z, I was the first hire at Fellows, an AI-focused fund, joining before ChatGPT changed everything. I started my career at ByteDance, the parent company of TikTok, where I worked on strategic investments across different product lines.
Outside of work, you'll find me on the tennis court, in a pilates or hot yoga class, or somewhere underwater scuba diving.

rows.name: Dan Remondi
lines: I'm a member of the Client Solutions & Services team at General Catalyst, where I engage with institutional investors and limited partners across our investment platform, with a particular focus on GC's Customer Value Fund.

Prior to joining GC, I spent four years in a similar capacity at KKR, where I discovered my passion for partnering with sophisticated investors as they navigate alternative investments and private markets. I began my career at Morgan Stanley's Global Capital Markets division in New York after graduating from Georgetown University with a degree in Economics.
When I'm not in the office, you'll find me chasing powder in the Rockies during winter or teeing off at the Bay Area's finest golf courses the rest of the year.

rows.name: Dan Riley
lines: I was inspired to study and practice law by my mother, an attorney who owns and operates her own law practice. Yet, I had a strong inclination towards business and entrepreneurship so was always looking for an opportunity to combine those interests.

After a great learning experience within WilmerHale’s corporate and securities practice, I continued my career at Gunderson Dettmer, where venture investing and emerging companies are the focus. It was during my time at Gunderson Dettmer that my passion for entrepreneurship and venture capital really blossomed. I’ll never forget the first time I had access to investment memos and could step into the minds of seasoned investors to understand how they valued and analyzed private companies. I quickly realized I was destined for a career at the intersection of law and venture capital.

I’m thrilled to join General Catalyst where I have the opportunity to work with our incredible team and impressive entrepreneurs to leverage my experience to streamline processes and reduce some of the legal friction around company fundraising and growth.

On the personal side, I enjoy spending time with my wife and young son. We spend our time traveling, exploring New England and enjoying our neighborhood in Charlestown. On the side, I’m learning yet another new industry by volunteering on the board of a local preschool and continue to patiently wait for the Buffalo Bills to win a Super Bowl.

rows.name: Darin Souza
lines: I’m a Wealth Manager at GC Wealth, a next-generation wealth management platform built for transformational individuals, families, and organizations, and a critical component of GC’s effort to go Beyond Venture. I’m based in Cambridge, MA.

I’ve served as a trusted advisor for founders, families, and institutions over the past two decades, and I’m excited to use GC Wealth’s proximity to General Catalyst to support my clients’ journeys. My team and I came to GC Wealth from First Republic, bringing a proactive, high-touch approach to client service.

Before entering wealth management, I served as an Infantry Officer in the U.S. Army, mostly with the 82nd Airborne Division, in various leadership and operations roles. It was there I learned the true meaning of “Mission first, people always.”

I attended the United States Military Academy at West Point and played baseball for Army. During my military service, I earned my Ranger Tab, Senior Jumpmaster designation, and several other certifications. After leaving the military, I earned my MBA from Dartmouth College’s Tuck School of Business.

My family of four lives in Cohasset, MA, and we’re actively involved in a wide range of community organizations. When we’re not on the sports sidelines, we enjoy wrestling with our dog, Lucky, and chasing our kids down the ski slopes.

rows.name: Daryl Tol
lines: I served for two decades in the C-suites of regional and national healthcare organizations, yet I describe my favorite work as helping patients find services they lack, discovering new forms of advocacy, and enhancing transparency. I see Health Assurance as a fundamental formula for human thriving, meaning there are many levers for reducing friction, inefficiency, and cost while increasing innovation, collaboration, and effectiveness of care.

At AdventHealth, where I ran one of the largest hospital systems in the US, my focus included identifying the frustrations patients should never endure, and then recasting them as a set of positive experiences patients should come to expect. With my national perspective embracing people, facilities, science, technology, finance, policies, and payments, I convened the conversations necessary for advancing this mission.

I’m now President of Health Assurance Transformation Company (HATCo),  a platform created by GC to transform health systems into resilient, vibrant organizations in partnership with leading technology companies and to achieve the promise of GC’s vision for health assurance: evolving healthcare from a “sick care” system to a proactive system designed to help people stay well, and make quality care more affordable and more accessible to all. In my role, I am responsible for driving, operationalizing, and expanding HATCo Services, a network of strategic partnerships with 23+ health systems and GC portfolio companies to share best practices, provide strategic advisory services, and scale impact to effect lasting change in the U.S. healthcare industry. In addition, HATCo has signed a definitive agreement to acquire Summa Health, to create a new system of community-based, lifelong healthcare to serve as a blueprint for broader healthcare transformation in the US and beyond.
Away from work, I get outdoors, preferably on the water or a mountain, or I travel to immerse myself in foreign cultures.

rows.name: Dave Breslin
lines: I lead our Wealth Managers and their associates in serving our wealth management clients as well as continuing to grow the ranks of advisors serving GC Wealth. I also carry responsibility for our operations, technology platform and focus on industry formation and new capabilities to best meet the needs of our clients and founders.

I joined GC in 2023, following seven years at First Republic and seventeen years at Merrill Lynch, where I held a variety of senior leadership positions. At First Republic, I played a key leadership role in the significant growth of First Republic Private Wealth Management and played an important part in the hiring of the more than 180 Wealth Managers across the country.

I graduated from the University of Vermont and completed The Wharton School’s Executive Development Program at the University of Pennsylvania in 2018. Alongside my work at GC, I dedicate considerable time to both the Make-A-Wish Foundation in the Bay Area and the Seal Future Foundation, where I mentor Navy SEAL Team members transitioning from military to civilian life. When I’m not at GC, you can find me alongside my wife Ashley and our dog Lou, canvassing one of the many beaches at the west end of San Francisco.
rows.title: EVP, GC Wealth

rows.name: David Fialkow
lines: As a venture capitalist and an academy award-winning documentary filmmaker / producer, I love working with creative people and helping them have real impact. Before Joel Cutler and I co-founded General Catalyst, we built and sold four companies, including National Leisure Group; Alliance Development Group; Retail Growth ATM Systems and Starboard Cruise Services (sold to LVMH).
My focus areas include financial services, digital health, AI, and data analytics.

Before business, I studied film at Colgate University, earned a law degree from Boston College, and made documentary films. My wife Nina and I still make documentaries focused on healthcare and social justice. Two of our documentary films have won Academy Awards. To explore others we have produced, click here.

I have raised millions of dollars for kids’ programs by biking, running, climbing, and rowing. I serve on nonprofit boards including Facing History and Ourselves, the Dean’s Advisory Council at the MIT School of Engineering, the Council on Foreign Relations, and the Pan-Mass Challenge (former chairman). I am also chair of the Investment Advisory Committee of The Engine at MIT and am a member of The MIT Corporation — the Institute’s board of trustees.
rows.title: Co-Founder & Managing Director

rows.name: Delany Higgins
lines: I serve as Director of Strategic Initiatives at General Catalyst Institute (GCI), where I support the team on founder-facing engagements and projects.

Before joining GCI, I was a Senior Policy Advisor at the White House National Economic Council on the economic security team. I have also worked on economic policy for Senator Rand Paul and the Senate Homeland Security Committee, and on foreign policy for former Senator Pat Toomey. I completed my undergraduate degree in Modern History and Art History at the University of St Andrews in Scotland and a master’s degree in International Political Economy at the London School of Economics.
In my free time, I enjoy trips with friends to the driving range, exploring what’s new in D.C., and hanging out with my cat, Mimi.

rows.name: Dory Bowers
lines: I’m Head of Operations for GC Wealth, leading the “engine room” of GC Wealth out of our Cambridge office. I handle our foundational wealth management platform, ensuring it’s flexible and accommodating to adapt to our clients’ needs while maintaining consistency, security, and transparency.

Before joining GC Wealth, I held several Operations leadership positions, where I built and scaled all components of high-growth investment management and advisory firms. I bring a keen analytical approach, using technology to streamline processes and maximize efficiency, allowing our wealth managers to concentrate on their clients and deliver a consistent experience.

I graduated from Smith College with a BA in Biology and dove into the field of cancer research at the Dana Farber Cancer Institute, focusing on hematological malignancies, before transitioning my problem-solving skills to the world of financial services. I’m an avid sailor who loves exploring rocky coasts around the world, with a strong preference for the waters of the Canadian Maritimes. On dry land, you’ll never see me far from my beloved pups Marion and Birdie.
rows.title: Head of Operations, GC Wealth

rows.name: Drake Pooley
lines: My career has been defined by understanding how to improve our world by perceiving system dynamics and acting decisively to change them for the better. My favorite moments are when I reach unexpected conclusions that require me to re-wire how I thought about an issue. Having traveled to 85 countries, it’s happened a lot. These are the moments I experience the most joy.

I’ve worked for a real estate firm in Shanghai, an energy company in Houston, a venture capital firm in Mexico, a growth stage startup in San Francisco, and an airline in the Middle East. I started my career building economic models at Kearney in New York and Dubai, a far cry from my childhood where my parents ran a surf shop in Texas (yes, there is surf in Texas).
I am the Chief of Staff at General Catalyst. In this role I support the CEO in advancing our strategy and develop our most important global relationships.

I started my educational journey in community college and ended it at Stanford University for my MBA, where I served as class president and received the top award at graduation as voted by my classmates. Along the way I completed my Bachelor’s at Auburn, a Master’s at the University of Virginia, and a Master’s at ESADE Business School. I live in New York, and write regularly, having been published in the New York Times, Washington Post, and others. I’m a dual US-Lithuanian citizen, and keep the American immigrant experience and the Lithuanian experience overcoming Soviet tyranny close at heart.
rows.title: Chief of Staff

rows.name: Drew Gordon
lines: I began serving sophisticated investors from the start of my career. At Morgan Stanley, I gained domain expertise in the global financial and real estate sectors while developing and articulating both long-term strategies and market-driven tactics for high-net-worth investors.

I then entered the fund placement industry with Campbell Lutyens, a global placement agent, where I advised leading private equity and venture capital financial sponsors on their institutional fundraising and capital formation initiatives. Through my experience with Campbell Lutyens, I learned to appreciate the importance of developing and managing an efficient capital-raising process while serving the complex needs of limited partners. My work caught the eye of General Catalyst, which brought me on board to join its Client Solutions & Services team.

I value the firm’s team-oriented, collaborative approach, where I can draw on my full range of prior experiences to help carry forward General Catalyst's mission of investing in powerful, positive change that endures. I’m excited to be on a team that raises capital with a purpose that extends beyond profit and seeks to form enduring relationships with limited partners who share in that vision.

Outside the office, I’m an avid sports fan and love to get outdoors. I played varsity lacrosse at Middlebury College and still play on occasion, but I’ve also picked up running, cycling, and pickleball to stay active.

rows.name: Dylan Spector
lines: I’m an investor on the Health Assurance team at General Catalyst, where I love working with ambitious, mission-driven founders from seed through growth stages and beyond. I’m most drawn to transformative healthcare companies that shift the focus from "sick care" to proactive wellness, innovatively reducing costs and making quality care more affordable and accessible for everyone.

Before joining GC, I spent time at the Boston Consulting Group, where I specialized in commercial due diligence and growth strategy work in life sciences, consumer healthcare, and enterprise software.

I graduated from Dartmouth College with a BA in Economics and Computer Science. While at Dartmouth, I was closely involved with managing The Dartmouth student newspaper, which included overseeing the launch of additional revenue streams and the creation of an endowment fund to support the paper in perpetuity.

Outside of the office, I enjoy staying active with boxing or pickup basketball, traveling to countries where I can work on my Spanish, and spending time with family and friends. I’m also actively involved with mentoring first-generation college students and love meeting new people from different corners of the world.

rows.name: Elena Viboch
lines: In the life sciences, every day holds the opportunity to transform medicine. I always wanted to be a scientist, and I became curious about the path that connects basic research to biotechnology products. That interest led me to a job with a biotech venture capital firm. I was able to work closely with entrepreneurs and help them bring their work from idea to execution to impact.

My experience gave me a lot of empathy for what it takes to commercialize biotechnology products. After holding corporate development and operations leadership roles, I joined SoftBank. I led a team focused on life science investing, over the course of three years helping to build the Vision Fund’s portfolio with 12 health technology investments.

I joined General Catalyst for the opportunity to help fulfill the promise of health assurances — investing in technology that provides access to affordable care and helps people stay well. As an investor, I’m always hoping to meet founders with a passion for transformative science who are working on problems that address significant unmet medical needs.

When founders go after hard technical challenges with the goal of saving lives, they can deliver meaningful change. I love working with founders who focus on delivering a positive impact on human health and creating lasting businesses.

My research focus was translational biology and I have an MS from Johns Hopkins, an MBA from Harvard and a BA from Swarthmore. I’m passionate about helping women in science to advance their careers and their companies. I love music and try to find opportunities to sing whenever I can, and I also enjoy swimming and hiking through the Bay Area.
rows.title: Managing Director

rows.name: Emma Lu
lines: Growing up in Canada as the child of Chinese immigrants, I learned first-hand the resilience and grit it takes to build something from scratch. It also meant nothing came with a default setting: I learned to look at everything with fresh eyes, rather than inheriting a sense of how things are supposed to be.

After graduating from the University of Pennsylvania with a B.S. in Finance & Statistics from Wharton and a B.A. in Computational Biology, I began my career at KKR on the infrastructure team in Menlo Park, covering data centers, aviation and transport, and renewable energy. What became clear was how much of the value creation in these industries would come from technology. That took me to TPG's minority tech growth fund, where I worked on AI and consumer investments in some of the best late-stage businesses in the world. Data centers and consumer were both quiet corners of the market then, and AI has since turned both into some of the most interesting opportunities.

I joined General Catalyst to back growth-stage founders rebuilding industries rather than optimizing their edges. I spend most of my time at the next frontier of consumer tech, but what I'm really drawn to is people who are early to a market others have written off and have the tenacity to stay there.
Outside the office, I'm most likely on the tennis court, in the mountains, or at an SF park with pastries.

rows.name: Erin Himel
lines: As Vice President of Experiential Marketing at General Catalyst, I oversee the company’s event strategy and focus on creating experiences that bring entrepreneurs, founders, business leaders, and policymakers together to connect, collaborate, and shape the future. At GC, events go beyond gatherings—they are catalysts for innovation, connection, and meaningful dialogue.

Before joining General Catalyst, I spent over a decade at Meta leading the Global Experiences team. I was fortunate to work alongside a talented group of creatives and marketers, delivering the company’s highest-profile events and product launches across its brand portfolio. From partnering with artists and global brands to working with small businesses, developers, and creators, I had the opportunity to bring stories to life for audiences around the world.

Originally from the Pacific Northwest, I’m now based in San Francisco. I have a passion for all things design—especially interior design—and love that my professional world intersects with my personal interests. Outside of work, you’ll find me discovering great food and exploring the outdoors.

rows.name: Federica Roth
lines: I am a Director at GC Wealth.
I joined GC in 2025 after spending five years on the investment team at Stanford Management Company, which manages Stanford University’s investment assets.
I hold a B.S. in Management Science and Engineering from Stanford University and an MPhil in Bioscience Enterprise from the University of Cambridge. I am also a CFA Charterholder.

rows.name: Gabriella Giglio
lines: People are sometimes surprised to learn that I was a dancer before entering the corporate world. To me, there are many parallels. Dancing requires focus, discipline and hard work, and every performance is meticulously choreographed to produce a specific effect. In business, every ambitious, growing organization needs to give high performers a well-designed framework for achieving their goals.

I started my career at American Express in Risk Management and Operations, and eventually transitioned to my calling: human resources.
