During my years with Amex, I provided HR partnership and expertise in the areas of: executive recruitment and talent planning; succession analysis; international HR & global employee relations; training & development; employee inclusion; organization effectiveness; mergers & acquisitions; and global leadership development.

I joined General Catalyst because of the people and the culture. I had the privilege of meeting everyone in the firm before I started and was inspired by their energy, potential, mission, and values. At many investment firms, there isn’t a focus on transformation solutions. But at GC, we are focused on developing powerful ecosystems which connects innovators with adopters. I am pleased to focus on organizational effectiveness and business performance with these teams.

I was born in Rome, raised in the U.S., and have worked in Asia and Europe. My parents were immigrants who instilled in me that anything is possible if you want it and work for it hard enough. That experience drives me to give back in multiple arenas: dance companies, protection for animals, and the development of future HR leaders through the CHRO Board Academy and the Wharton Financial Services Group. If I’m not in a meeting or at an event, you might find me working out at Bar Method or running in the great outdoors with my husband, Steven.
rows.title: Chief Transformation Officer

rows.name: Gosia Majczak
lines: I am an investor at General Catalyst's Berlin office, where I drive the firm's Global Resilience thesis across Europe. In an era defined by increasing global crises and great power competition, I focus on backing founders who are modernizing critical infrastructure across climate and energy, industrials, and defense and intelligence sectors. I work on both traditional venture investments and the Creation strategy, where I help build thesis-driven companies from the ground up to address critical gaps in Europe's industrial and technological landscape.

Before joining GC, I was a strategy consultant at McKinsey & Company, where I helped major industrial and consumer companies navigate their sustainability and digital transformation journeys. This experience gave me firsthand insight into Europe's industrial challenges, from rising energy costs to workforce shortages, and the opportunities for innovative solutions. I also served as an advisor to the United Nations, working on economic development and environmental initiatives. Combined with my MA in Quantitative Methods from Columbia University and BASc in Economics and Mathematics from University College London, this diverse background helps me bring a fresh perspective to identifying and supporting promising startups.

When I’m not meeting with founders or diving deep into new technologies, you'll find me exploring my creative side through product design, film, and photography. I bring this creative mindset to my work with entrepreneurs, helping them think differently about solving complex industrial challenges.

I am particularly excited to connect with founders and industry leaders who share my vision of building a more resilient and technologically sovereign Europe, whether through traditional venture investments or creative company-building approaches.

rows.name: Hannah Lique Naitove
lines: I am a Senior Operations Associate for GC Wealth at General Catalyst, where I support internal business operations, coordinate teams cross-functionally, and drive processes and efficiency initiatives. Based in Cambridge, MA, my focus is on building scalable systems and operational frameworks that enhance collaboration and enable our team to deliver exceptional service to our clients.

Prior to joining GC Wealth, I worked as a Senior Client Relationship Associate, supporting high-net-worth individuals and delivering white glove client service. Earlier in my career, I held compliance and operations roles at registered investment advisory firms. I have also owned and operated a date night planning business, combining creativity and logistics to deliver memorable experiences for clients.

I earned a Bachelor’s degree in Economics with a minor in Business Management from Keene State College. When I’m not in the office, you can find me playing soccer, basketball, or figure skating. I also enjoy discovering unique experiences, traveling, visiting new coffee shops, and trying new restaurants.

rows.name: Harry Elliott
lines: I am a British native and former Stanford intercollegiate debater. I believe in the beginner’s mentality: starting from first principles and basic questions to achieve decisive clarity on problems that are new or have few historical precedents.

After Stanford, I put this mentality to work at Goldman Sachs, where I developed new and customized financing solutions for emerging asset classes and younger companies that traditionally wouldn't seek out bank debt. I then moved to Verkada, a growth-stage security business that had reached product-market fit and was ready to scale. As Director of Demand Generation, I drove Verkada’s growth across regions and sales channels through a combination of quantitative analysis and creative experimentation.

At General Catalyst, I bring my blend of financial analysis and operating company experience to help growth-stage companies scale quickly and tackle demand generation challenges. Away from the office, I enjoy hiking in Northern California with my wife and two dogs and working on weekend DIY projects.

rows.name: Hemant Taneja
lines: I am the CEO of General Catalyst.

My work centers on applied AI as the engine for abundance and resilience—modernizing the systems that matter most to society. I laid out my thesis for building resilient, abundant systems in my 2025 national bestseller: The Transformation Principles.

I have architected GC’s strategy to drive global resilience through AI transformation in five critical industries: healthcare, defense, industrials, energy, and financial services. General Catalyst provides its portfolio founders with powerful advantages to execute this strategy, including a flexible capital stack, market access through its operating businesses like HATCo and Percepta, global policy expertise via the GC Institute, and the GC Famiglia, a global ecosystem of relationships.

As an investor, I have backed many generational founders who have built market leading companies like Anduril, Anthropic, Applied Intuition, Gusto, Long Lake, Polymarket, Ro, Samsara, Snap and Stripe.

I also co-founded several companies—including Commure, Hippocratic AI, Livongo (sold to Teladoc for $18.5Bn) and Transcarent—that are part of my vision for transforming the healthcare industry into a proactive, affordable, and accessible system.
I'm the author of four books and hold five degrees from MIT: M.Eng. EECS, S.M. Operations Research, S.B. Biology, S.B. Mathematics, and S.B. EECS.
Hemant Taneja's Latest Book 'The Transformation Principles' is Available Now
Seeding the Future with The Interaction Company of California
rows.title: CEO

rows.name: Henry Kline
lines: With a cardiothoracic and vascular surgeon as parents, I practically grew up in the hospital, but rather than become a doctor (sorry Mom & Dad), I chose to focus on transforming how care is delivered. I am passionate about improving patient outcomes and consumer health experiences through technology and innovation, working to bridge the gap between clinical excellence and scalable solutions that make care more accessible, personalized, and effective.

At General Catalyst, I invest in growth-stage businesses and partner with exceptional teams to help them scale. I focus on supporting companies as they enter their next phase of expansion, building on the strength of durable unit economics and clear product-market fit, while deepening their impact on the customers and consumers. I also founded Pride@GC to ensure everyone feels at home and their truest selves at work.

Before GC, I worked at AEA Investors, an upper middle-market private equity firm, where I invested across consumer and healthcare services companies. I initially began my career in M&A and restructuring at Lazard, helping the world’s largest companies navigate complexity and avoid downside.

I graduated from Harvard College with a degree in Applied Mathematics and Computer Science, and after a couple years, I headed back to Cambridge to get my MBA at Harvard Business School. I am now back home in New York, where I was born and raised. In my downtime, you can find me outdoors, hiking or skiing (probably listening to some country music), playing tennis, crafting, or watching Michigan sports.

rows.name: Hirsh Jain
lines: I am the Co-founder & CEO of Percepta (a GC Transformation Company) that combines applied AI engineering with frontier research to transform enterprises. Unlike traditional AI point solutions or consulting engagements, Percepta embeds AI engineers, researchers, and product managers directly within organizations.

I spent the last seven years at Palantir Technologies, where I led the healthcare and civilian government business and served as Senior Vice President. I care deeply about bringing new technologies to long‑neglected domains and building enduring institutions that serve the public good.

Before Palantir, I also held technology roles at Google, Jane Street, and within the U.S. Department of Defense. I was also a published machine learning author and studied Computer Science and Mathematics at Harvard.
rows.title: Co-founder & CEO, Percepta

rows.name: Holly Maloney
lines: Head of Health Assurance & Managing Director

I lead General Catalyst’s Health Assurance strategy. I invest across all stages and sectors in healthcare, with a focus on AI-native companies modernizing care delivery, value-based care infrastructure, and the platforms that will enable a health system that is proactive, affordable, and accessible for all.

I believe that now is the time for transformative action in U.S. healthcare. After decades of fragmentation, rising costs, and uneven outcomes, there is an unprecedented opportunity to create a healthcare system that delivers for everyone through innovative technology. The U.S. is on the cusp of meaningful consumer and provider enablement, powered by healthcare-specific clinical AI companies that are built to navigate the complexities of American healthcare.

While trained as a growth stage investor, I now invest across all stages. I enjoy bringing the lessons from more mature businesses to companies in the early stages of product-market fit, while also helping growth stage companies stay connected to the startup innovation happening around them.

I came to healthcare after a decade investing in software and technology companies. I began my career at Guidepost Growth Equity, where I developed a thesis of investing in highly scalable businesses in industries undergoing digital transformation. I later discovered a passion for collaborating with successful management teams while advising technology companies at AGC. Now, I apply those lessons — navigating complex industry transformation while working hand-in-hand alongside founders and executives — to healthcare.

I am a member of the Board of Trustees and Investment Committee of Bowdoin College and a Board Member of All Raise. I live in Marin County with my partner Mike, our two daughters Quinn and Riley, and our dog Bo. I enjoy competitive active sports, including running, hiking, and biking. I'm also now learning to surf and welcome your advice on the best breaks.
rows.title: Head of Health Assurance & Managing Director

rows.name: Jack Cohen
lines: Today, I serve as the VP of Marketing Operations at General Catalyst. I joined GC in mid-2022 as VP of Content & Engagement to rethink the organization's global content strategy and building out our global events team and strategy.

Prior to GC, I spent five years at FirstMark, a New-York based venture firm, where I learned under one of the pioneering Platform leaders—Dan Kozikowski. My legacy product was called Guilds—a product & set of communities for CXOs across the top companies in tech—scaling it from dozens of portfolio leaders to well over 1,500+ CXOs across 700+ of the best companies in tech—public and private. The core focus of the Guilds was to provide venture-backed startup leaders with impactful communities, resources, and playbooks to better themselves and the organizations they lead. I also launched a program called 'Public School' — a curriculum-style bootcamp for ~50 pre-IPO founders & CFOs getting ready to hit the public markets.

Before FirstMark, I began my career as an operator on the early-stage startup side, helping scale Blue Apron (the once high-flying category creator) from a regional to national brand and through an IPO as Head of Community. Ultimately, I grew Blue Apron’s community from 75K to over 2.5M home chefs nationwide by the time I left. All the while, constantly leveraging new platforms with creative and dedicated strategies.

When I'm not helping founders build enduring businesses, you can find me exploring New York with a camera in hand, fly fishing, playing tennis, or simply enjoying a walk with my wife and mini dachshund, Gus, in our neighborhood of Brooklyn Heights. Finally, to give back, I mentor college students as they prepare to enter the 'real world' and am a member of Big Brother, Big Sister NYC where I mentored a young boy in the Bronx.

rows.name: Jack Horgan
lines: I am a Relationship Manager at GC Wealth, General Catalyst’s dedicated platform for partnering with families, founders, and institutions. With over 20 years of experience across portfolio consulting, wealth strategy, financial planning, and relationship management, I bring a holistic perspective to every client relationship.
My approach is grounded in building long-term trust, simplifying complexity, and aligning financial decisions with client values.

I graduated from Santa Clara University with a Bachelor of Science in Combined Sciences and a minor in Political Science. I am a CFA charterholder and a CFP® professional. Outside of work, I enjoy traveling with my wife and children, attending concerts, and pursuing my passion for motorsport — whether trackside at a race or in a sim racing cockpit.

rows.name: Jakob Mökander
lines: I serve as Vice President, Policy – Europe & UK at the General Catalyst Institute. In practice, this means that I help founders scale transformative companies and advise governments on how to build innovation ecosystems that drive long-term prosperity and security.

An engineer turned social scientist, I have spent my career exploring how technology shapes societies and how innovation can be directed toward public value. That journey has taken me from Sweden through Germany, Austria, the US, the UK and India – including Delhi, where I met my wife.

Before joining GC, I was Director of Science & Technology Policy at the Tony Blair Institute. Working closely with the former UK prime minister, I built and led a team advising political leaders in more than 40 countries on AI adoption, research funding and digital sovereignty.

Earlier, I worked at McKinsey & Co in London, driving digital transformation in Fortune 500 companies, and at the Swedish Trade & Invest Council in New Delhi, building partnerships between government and industry in India. I also served in the Swedish Armed Forces, leading a platoon and sleeping long stretches in the Arctic forest – at times under northern lights.

I hold a DPhil from the University of Oxford, where my research focused on AI governance. While in academia, I developed the world's first end-to-end framework for auditing large language models – which has since been piloted and adopted by major AI labs. I have been a Visiting Scholar at Princeton University and remain affiliated with Yale's Digital Ethics Center.
Outside of work, I read history and philosophy, play racket sports and design houses. The Swedish summer cottage I built with my family remains my favourite place on earth.

rows.name: James Gersack
lines: I am a Wealth Manager at GC Wealth, a next-generation wealth management platform created by General Catalyst as they endeavor Beyond Venture. My team and I support entrepreneurs throughout their wealth journey with disciplined investment and planning expertise, emphasizing tax efficiency, liquidity, and transparency.

Before joining General Catalyst, I served as Managing Director at First Republic Private Wealth Management and as President of First Western Trust, both in Jackson Hole, WY. Prior to that, I worked at Montgomery Securities and Sanford C. Bernstein (Bernstein Private Wealth), both in San Francisco, CA.

I graduated from Montana State University with a degree in Finance and Economics and from Franciscan University of Steubenville with a degree in Theology. I also hold the Certified Financial Planner (CFP®) designation from the Certified Financial Planner Board of Standards. My wife, Jenny, and I have two children, Emma (15) and Lucas (11). I also serve as a Trustee of the Hughes Charitable Foundation.

rows.name: James Wilcox
lines: I am a Wealth Manager at GC Wealth based in Jackson Hole, WY. At GC Wealth, I manage investment portfolios for clients with the fiduciary standard of offering only independent advice. In our multi-family office structure, I advise on liquidity management and longer-term tax and estate strategies.

Prior to joining General Catalyst, I worked at First Republic Investment Management in Los Angeles, CA, and Jackson, WY from 2018 to 2023. I also spent time at Goldman Sachs in New York, NY, and Los Angeles, CA from 1999 to 2018. Additionally, I served as the Press Secretary to US House Ways and Means Chairperson Bill Archer of Texas from 1995 to 1998. I graduated from Middlebury College in 1994 and earned my MBA from Columbia Business School in 2000.

Outside of work, I am the Board Chair of the non-profit Coombs Outdoors, the Board Chair of the Jackson Hole Community School, and a volunteer firefighter and Emergency Medical Responder for Jackson Hole EMS. My wife Lindsay and I have four children and two dogs, a French Bulldog (Hazel) and a Great Dane (Odie).

rows.name: Jeannette zu Fürstenberg
lines: I am the President and a Managing Director of the global VC firm General Catalyst (GC), where I am in charge of its European business. I am also a Founding Partner of La Famiglia VC, one of Europe’s most distinguished early-stage Venture Capital platforms connecting the established industry and the start-up ecosystem. The merging of La Famiglia with General Catalyst has expanded my seed investment activity to a global level.

I embody the role of a passionate generalist with a founder-led approach. My investments are driven by my vision of a resilient, more prosperous Europe, with technology as a key driver of transformation. This vision is reflected in my areas of expertise, including AI, climate, industrial transformation, defense, and traditional software-centric opportunities. Some of my early investment wins include companies such as Deel, Forto, Helsing, Mistral, and Personio. Having supported their journey since the earliest stages of ideation, I also serve on the board of the unicorn companies Helsing and Mistral.

Beyond my investment activities, I am an active member of advisory boards for various companies and organizations, including serving on the Board of Governors of the Kiel Institute for the World Economy (ifw). I am committed to strengthening the connections between the tech ecosystem and established industries, which I demonstrate by hosting exclusive events aimed at creating a platform to facilitate these interactions. My engagement extends to the political sphere through various lobbying efforts to foster a conducive environment for entrepreneurship in Europe. Notably, I have contributed to the debate on the EU AI Act and addressed several socio-economic issues related to European prosperity.

I am a regular guest at distinguished events and conferences such as ITW, the Resilience Conference, and the Berlin Global Dialogue, where I emphasize topics such as European sovereignty and technology advancement. More recently, I moderated a roundtable discussion on Applied AI hosted by French President Emmanuel Macron and German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, featuring AI experts from industry, academia, and the public sector.
In 2011, I initiated “Fürstenberg Zeitgenössisch”, a contemporary art foundation and artist grant program. I hold a PhD in Philosophy and Entrepreneurship from Freie Universität Berlin.
The Decade Space Stops Being Hard
rows.title: President & Managing Director

rows.name: Jennifer Zimmerman
lines: One of the best experiences of my advertising career was being employee #8 in a start-up agency with audacious ambitions and convincing big advertisers that our merry band of creatives could transform a big global brand without breaking it. I quickly grew into the strategy role because I could pick up a clean sheet of paper and a Sharpie and, working with the same source material as everyone else, come up with completely different insights. Ultimately, we won major accounts with American Express, Disney, Intel, Hershey’s, Marriott, and many other well-known brands.

Along the way, I learned that successful company formation is like being in a jazz group. Everyone has to be able to play tightly together and also improvise completely new riffs on cue. There’s no conductor – everyone in the group is a player. So when General Catalyst asked me to join the firm as CMO, it felt more like joining a new band than switching industries. That combination of creativity and collaboration has been in the firm’s DNA from the beginning.

Another draw is the ‘maker mentality’ that pervades everything we do at General Catalyst. This is so liberating for a marketer because the companies we support are doing such creative, out-of-the-box work already. If anything, the challenge is telling those stories in a way that’s just as creative and unexpected as the companies themselves. My vision is that our brand and those of our portfolio companies will become a powerful, valuable asset and a point of pride for customers, investors, and employees.

Away from work, my great loves are words, language, and the outdoors. To keep my problem-solving mind sharp, I complete the New York Times crossword puzzle every day. Once I’m outside hiking, biking, or skiing, the language of nature takes over. And whenever I can, I take the time to mentor other women and give back the wisdom I have received from so many others.
rows.title: Special Advisor

rows.name: Jeremy Parsels
lines: I am a Wealth Manager at GC Wealth, dedicated to serving the unique financial needs of founders, entrepreneurs, executives, and multi-generational families. With a deep understanding of financial markets, I deliver tailored, comprehensive solutions that help our clients preserve, grow, and transition their wealth across generations.

My core focus is on investment and portfolio management, providing holistic and tailored advice that incorporates tax planning, pre- and post- liquidity strategies, and the intricacies of multi-asset balance sheets. I work with founders and executives to support them at each stage of their financial journey—from company formation and critical liquidity events, to legacy planning and philanthropic giving.

Prior to joining General Catalyst, I spent over 20 years in wealth and investment management at institutions including J.P. Morgan, First Republic Bank, Merrill Lynch, and Cambridge Associates. I am a graduate of the Pamplin College of Business at Virginia Tech and a Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA) charterholder.

rows.name: Jessica Hale
lines: Chief Legal & Compliance Officer, GC Wealth

I am the Chief Legal and Compliance Officer for GC Wealth, a next-generation wealth management platform built for transformational individuals, families, and organizations and a critical component of GC’s endeavor to go Beyond Venture.

After working in the investment management department at Ropes & Gray LLP, I went in-house to work for a client and loved the experience of building the business in partnership with colleagues. After helping the firm set up multiple offices outside of the United States, in addition to my legal work, I took on the role of Global Chief Compliance Officer, which nicely complemented my love of travel. I then joined the legal department at First Republic Bank, where, after several years providing legal coverage for Private Wealth Management, I ultimately became Chief Compliance Officer for First Republic Investment Management.

I am a proud graduate of The Ohio State University, for which I serve on the Political Science Alumni Advisory Board, as well as The Boston University School of Law. In addition to cheering on the Buckeyes, I am a Giants baseball fan and an avid reader, always happy to discuss books. I live on one of San Francisco’s many hills with my husband, two children, and beloved mutt.
rows.title: Chief Legal & Compliance Officer, GC Wealth

rows.name: Jim Cash
lines: My current focus is on digital transformation, and understanding how large scale enterprises can use emerging technologies to accelerate that transformation. The challenge is sustaining growth and innovation while their business models evolve, new regulations such as ESG and privacy mandates are introduced, and continuously evolving cybersecurity risks must be effectively managed.

The early part of my career was spent as an academic, serving Harvard Business School (HBS) as a Professor and Senior Associate Dean.  My last two roles were Chairman of the MBA program and Chairman of the Harvard Business School Publishing Company. During 2020 HBS designated a building to become The Cash House. My non-academic activity included serving on public, private and not-for-profit boards, including Wal-Mart, Chubb, General Electric, Microsoft, Sprint, Scientific Atlanta, State Street Corporation, Alcon Labs, Knight Ridder, Tandy (renamed Radio Shack), National Association of Basketball Coaches Foundation, Gardner Museum, Partners Healthcare, The Smithsonian National Museum of African American History and Culture and Mass General Hospital.  I am currently a director for AURA, WELL, and The Boston Celtics, while serving as an Advisor for Grain Management.

Under the umbrella of The Cash Catalyst, LLC, I provide development programs for executives interested in the intersection of technology and business strategy. These membership programs assist senior technology executives and board members in addressing the challenges that have arisen from the digitization of traditional business environments.

While I love all sports, basketball is what I most enjoy watching. I graduated from Texas Christian University with a BS in Mathematics, while being named an Academic All-American in basketball.  My jersey was retired by the university in 2011 and a statue was dedicated in 2022. I received a Master of Science in Computer Science from Purdue University's Graduate School of Mathematical Sciences; and a Doctor of Philosophy in Management Information Systems (MIS) and Accounting from Purdue University's Krannert Graduate School of Management.  I have received several honorary doctorate degrees, was selected as a Fellow of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences, was inducted into the Texas Sports Hall of Fame, Southwest Conference Hall of Fame, and the NCAA Academic All-American Hall of Fame.

rows.name: Joel Cutler
lines: As a founder, mentor and venture capital investor, I support young entrepreneurs for their entire start-up journey. I love big ideas and being able to establish leaders in a new field that isn’t already saturated with a flock of similar companies. If you’re going into a market or a region where others got there first, you can’t be just a little better. To be a leader, you have to be at least ten times better. Better yet is charting new territory. Then you get to define a space, make something out of nothing and define leadership.

I spent my entrepreneurial career building travel, specialty/targeted consumer-direct commerce and consumer fintech businesses before starting General Catalyst with my friend David Fialkow. That experience has served me well in helping entrepreneurs build really new and next-generation consumer products and services.

In the early days of General Catalyst, I was fortunate to partner with Paul English and Steve Hafner to start KAYAK in our offices to provide consumers with an easy and transparent way to purchase travel services online.

I like working with great teams that relentlessly focus on creating real inflection points in consumer experiences. One of my favorite things is to think through the confluence of new technology platforms and disruptive business models that can be the foundation of new consumer experiences. Sample companies currently involved with: Multiverse, Empathy, Warby Parker (NYSE: WRBY), Sesame Health, WellDot, Perk, Zego, Beauty Pie, Blank Street Coffee. Sample past companies include: Airbnb (NASDAQ:ABNB), Lemonade (NYSE:LMND), Oscar Health (NYSE:OSCR), KAYAK (IPO and acquired by Booking (NASDAQ: BKNG), ITA Software (acquired by Google), Handy (acquired by ANGI), OLX (acquired by Naspers), Venmo (part of PayPal).

I graduated from Colby College and Boston College Law School. Along with the boards of companies I am involved with, I also serve on the boards of Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, Boston Children’s Hospital Trust, and NYU Stern Tech MBA Advisory Board.
rows.title: Co-Founder & Managing Director

rows.name: Joey Chan
lines: I work on the Strategy and Execution team at the Health Assurance Transformation Company (HATCo). My focus is on transformation planning and developing an enabling vehicle to advise and spread HATCo's transformation thesis – that a true partnership between caregivers, innovators, and capital will help healthcare organizations become more vibrant and sustainable, and better equipped to serve everyone in their communities with greater impact.

Before joining HATCo, I held several positions at the Cleveland Clinic Health System in the Ohio and Florida markets starting in 2014. I began as an administrative fellow and was later appointed as the enterprise’s first Director of Workforce Planning and Integration, where I developed and executed workforce strategies for over 27,000 nursing caregivers and integrated seven acquired hospitals into the nursing enterprise. Most recently, I served as a senior director to activate, operate, and scale clinical/provider operations in Cleveland Clinic’s new Florida market.

I graduated from the University of California, Berkeley with a BA in Economics. During my time at Cal, I chaired and grew the International Student’s Advisory Committee, which focuses on service and advocacy. I then received my master’s degree with a concentration in Healthcare Management from Yale University, where I also served as a senator on the Yale Graduate Student Assembly.

Growing up playing rugby, I admire the physicality and humility of the sport. I now reside in Florida with my wife and our toddler. You’ll often find us going for a walk in the park with our son and soliciting parenting advice.

rows.name: John O. Utendahl
lines: President of Impact Initiatives & Managing Director

I serve as the President of Impact Initiatives at General Catalyst. I am a seasoned financial services executive and investment banker with over 40 years of experience in the field. In 2023, I retired from my most recent role as the Chairman of the Global Corporate and Investment Bank for Bank of America (BofA). At BofA, I served as the Senior Client Relationship Executive and trusted advisor to C-Suite and Board of Directors leadership at major corporations across various sectors such as industrials, media & telecommunications, financial services & insurance, technology & software, healthcare & pharmaceuticals, aviation, and private equity. As the Chairman, I was accountable for bringing the full power of the bank's global capabilities (banking, markets and advisory) to assist the largest clients by creating innovative solutions for their most significant financial opportunities. I was the lead advisor for over 40 of the bank's most significant and important corporate clients. In addition, I played an active role throughout my tenure at BofA as an advocate for diversity and inclusion in all facets of the bank's operations.

Immediately prior to joining Bank of America, I pioneered the role of Vice Chairman at Deutsche Bank. Again, using C-Suite and Board Member relationships, I established the position and implemented a client relationship management strategy that successfully integrated the senior advisor role into the account team structure. I was able to capitalize upon Deutsche Bank's global platform to create international opportunities for numerous corporate clients.

Before these senior positions at major investment banks, I spent almost two decades as Chairman of the Utendahl Financial Organization, consisting of a broker-dealer, corporate finance advisory and asset management, and established several private equity and real estate funds. The Utendahl Financial Organization was built from Utendahl Capital Partners, LP, established in 1992 - the largest minority-owned financial organization in the country for many years.

I began my career at Salomon Brothers in 1982 as a corporate bond trader and later became a trading desk manager in Merrill Lynch's corporate bond department. I have also served as a Director on several Boards, including the Securities Industry Association (SIA), the U.S. Fund for UNICEF and Big Brothers/Big Sisters. I received a BS degree in Business from Long Island University and an MBA in finance from Columbia University's Graduate School of Business, where I was also honored as the keynote speaker at the graduation ceremonies in 1994.
rows.title: President of Impact Initiatives & Managing Director

rows.name: Jon Rehagen
lines: As Chief Information Officer, I strategically oversee the information architecture, technology foundation, and operational backbone that power General Catalyst's evolution from a venture capital firm into a global transformation company. My broad mandate includes all aspects of IT Infrastructure, Cybersecurity, Data Governance, Real Estate, and Operational Security across all business lines.

My role is to ensure that General Catalyst's information systems and physical operating environment are secure, resilient, and actively enable the firm's global expansion and investment strategy. I have been instrumental in scaling the operational platform that supports the firm's transformation, efficiently translating macro-level business strategy into secure, stable systems.

With significant tenure, my hands-on experience has been pivotal to the firm's growth. My work established the enduring methodology for operational excellence, built on early contributions like setting up the foundational technology for leaders who went on to form companies such as KAYAK and Datalogix.

I approach my role as a strategic partner, relying on strong, systematic methodologies balanced with the flexibility required in a dynamic venture environment. This leadership style—rooted in my background as an IT consultant and the pragmatic values from my Maine upbringing—prioritizes transparent communication, risk mitigation, and continuous operational improvement.
I hold a degree in Management Information Systems from Newbury College.
When not focused on optimizing global information strategy and operational security, I enjoy road trips, cooking, gardening, and playing soccer with my family.
rows.title: Chief Technology Officer

rows.name: Jonathan Hartley
lines: I am a Wealth Manager at GC Wealth, where I partner with clients to navigate the complexities of their wealth, building relationships based on trust and a deep understanding of their unique goals. I combine a personalized approach with disciplined investment solutions. My focus is on pre- and post-liquidity planning, comprehensive reporting and managing portfolios with an emphasis on tax efficiency and transparent advice.

Before joining GC Wealth, I held wealth management positions at JPMorgan and First Republic Bank. My early career also included various consulting and advisory roles, which laid the foundation for working with founders, executives, and families in the technology and venture capital ecosystems.

I graduated from Virginia Tech and am a Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA) charterholder. Away from the office, you can often find me with my two children, coaching little league, and spending time outdoors.

rows.name: Jonny Zhang
lines: When I got to Harvard, I got to work. While studying both economics and computer science, I rose from an account management position to the lead of Harvard Student Agencies (HAS), a collection of student-run start-ups with 700 employees. This was during the COVID-19 pandemic, when even established businesses across industries were struggling to adapt.

Fortunately for HAS, I combine my entrepreneurial instincts with operational discipline, which allowed me to both identify and execute successful strategies. I also recognized a critical difference between economic challenges and programming puzzles: the former involve people, who need more than airtight logic to function effectively. Putting my team members in a position to succeed individually was fundamental to the collaborative success of the entire enterprise.

Somehow, I also found time to help teach Harvard’s introductory computer science course and pursue my long-time passion for video games. My in-depth experience with gaming led to an invitation to help General Catalyst assess investment theses in the video game industry. I then joined the firm to develop investments in the next generation of games as they incorporate more advanced levels of AI, ML, and user-generated content.

Although I have less time for personal gaming now, I still keep my hand in. I also enjoy musical theater, catching traveling shows in Boston and Broadway shows in New York, and I’m already thinking about what I can give back to the educational system and the teachers it depends on.

rows.name: Joseph Mathews
lines: I am a Wealth Manager at GC Wealth, based in Cambridge, MA, where I provide comprehensive planning to GC Wealth clients across the full scope of their financial picture and all stages of wealth creation. I focus on identifying high-consequence planning opportunities with the goal of maximizing my clients’ lifetime wealth potential. I am passionate about setting up consolidated, organized financial pictures to support our team’s concierge approach, ensuring clients maintain a transparent understanding of their financial journey.
I take a proactive, disciplined approach to implementing specific plans that create "day-to-day leverage" for my clients, allowing them more time to focus on their life priorities.

I’ve worked in Wealth Management since 2011 and joined GC Wealth from First Republic, bringing with me an extraordinary client service heritage combined with a scalable, modern platform for emerging wealth clients.

I’m a significant contributor to GC Wealth’s industry-leading adoption of wealth technology, and I firmly believe there’s no better place to innovate in our industry than from inside GC. I also routinely collaborate with tech founders to build innovative capabilities that transform our industry.
In my free time, I enjoy traveling to New England with my family, skiing, golfing, and mountain biking.
I graduated from The University of Vermont and am a Certified Financial Planner™.

rows.name: Josh Real
lines: I’m VP, Commercial Counsel at General Catalyst where I provide strategic legal guidance and help our teams and transformation companies navigate complex commercial and technology transactions. My work often involves bridging legal and business considerations to craft practical, scalable solutions as companies grow and evolve.

What drew me to GC and continues to energize me is the opportunity to be part of a team that’s not only investing in companies but also building transformational ones. I’m especially excited by and focused on the work we’re doing through our transformation companies such as HATCo, our Health Assurance Transformation Company, which partners with leading health systems to drive long-term, systemic change in healthcare. It's a bold, collaborative model focused on aligning incentives, enabling innovation, and improving outcomes and it’s exactly the kind of ambitious effort I’m proud to support.

Before joining GC, I advised clients across the technology, healthcare, and life sciences sectors in both in-house and law firm roles. Most recently, I was Counsel at Latham & Watkins where I advised on and drove strategic deals involving technology, IP, partnerships, and commercialization. Prior to that, I served as Assistant General Counsel and Director of Business Development at Everly Health, a digital health company, where I structured and closed complex commercial and technology partnerships, helped launch new products and enter new channels, and streamlined commercial legal operations. Earlier in my career, I practiced at both Willkie Farr & Gallagher and Paul Hastings, where I focused on technology transactions and IP matters.
I earned my J.D. from the University of Chicago and a B.A. in Neuroscience from the University of Southern California.

Outside of work, I enjoy spending time with my high school sweetheart (now wife) and our daughter, trying to maximize quality time with our daughter while she's still young enough to think we're fun and cool, rooting for USC athletics (especially football) and San Francisco sports teams, and staying active through running, the occasional boxing or Muay Thai workout, or catching a SoulCycle class with my wife.

rows.name: Kate Bender
lines: At General Catalyst, I’m part of GC’s Creation team, which focuses on incubations, transformations, and venture buyouts. I love working with founders and management teams to grow their companies, whether it’s through adopting new technology or acquiring new partners. Specifically, I invest in forward-thinking founders and owners of services companies who see a generational opportunity to transform their industry with frontier automation and intelligence capabilities.

Before joining GC, I was an investor at the private equity firm Altamont Capital Partners, where I invested in a variety of spaces—ranging from launching a new insurance carrier to buying an ice cream company. Prior to Altamont, I worked as a consultant at BCG.

I graduated from Stanford University with a BA in History and a Minor in Economics. I wrote my honors thesis on funding models in public education and earned an MA in Education from Stanford. I also received my MBA from the Stanford Graduate School of Business.

rows.name: Kate Walsh
lines: I serve as the Chair of the Board of Directors of Summa Health, which was acquired in October 2025 by Health Assurance Transformation Company (HATCo). HATCo is a platform created by global investment and transformation company General Catalyst to transform health systems into resilient, vibrant organizations in partnership with leading technology companies. Together, HATCo and Summa Health are embarking on a long-term vision to create a new, more proactive, accessible, and affordable system of community-based, lifelong healthcare.

My leadership spans both state-level healthcare policy and safety-net healthcare delivery. I bring a rare combination of executive capability and grounded empathy shaped by my time leading Boston Medical Center and most recently as Massachusetts Secretary of Health and Human Services, where I led the Executive Office of Health and Human Services (EOHHS), which provides access to medical and behavioral health care, long-term services and supports, and key nutritional and financial benefits. I represented a team of more than 21,000 staff across 11 agencies and the MassHealth system, who work daily to provide services and programs for nearly 1 in every 3 Massachusetts residents.

Prior to my appointment to Governor Healey’s cabinet, I served as CEO of the Boston Medical Center (BMC) health system for 13 years, overseeing an annual operating revenue of $6 billion. The BMC health system is comprised of a 514 bed, academic medical center that is the primary teaching affiliate of Boston University Chobanian & Avedisian School of Medicine, as well as WellSense Health Plan, a Medicaid Managed Care Organization, and Boston HealthNet, a network affiliation of 14 community health centers.

Before my time at BMC, I served as Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer of Brigham and Women’s Hospital, Chief Operating Officer for Novartis Institutes for Biomedical Research, and at Massachusetts General Hospital in positions including Senior Vice President of Medical Services and the MGH Cancer Center. Prior to my tenure at Mass General, I held positions in a number of New York City hospitals including Montefiore, Columbia Presbyterian Medical Center, Saint Luke’s – Roosevelt Hospital Center and the New York City Health and Hospitals Corporation.

I received my Bachelor of Arts and Master of Public Health degrees from Yale University. I have served as a member of the Board of the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston, the Boston Public Health Commission, the Massachusetts Hospital Association, the Association of American Medical Colleges, Pine Street Inn, and Yale University.

rows.name: Katie Keller
lines: I am happiest when I have the opportunity to learn from others. This drive for human connection, and for knowledge not yet published in textbooks, first led me to journalism. In college, when I wasn’t building software, I could be found running around Palo Alto interviewing local government officials for the Stanford Daily. I relished the process of uncovering the truth, whether the answer was at the end of a program run or buried in an interview transcript.

After graduating from Stanford with a Master’s in CS and a Bachelor’s in Econ, I started my career in the Salesforce Associate Product Manager (APM) program. I loved the combination of EQ and IQ that PM demanded — customer empathy was just as important as technical aptitude. My most gratifying moments were when I was able to unblock someone at work, both by shipping features for customers and automating mundane work for my developer team.

APMs tend to be entrepreneurial. As many of my Salesforce APM colleagues left to start their own companies, I became fascinated with the startup ecosystem. I made the jump into venture capital to support founders like them in any way I could. I started my venture career at Menlo Ventures, where I formed lasting relationships with founders building companies in AI, infrastructure, consumer social, electric vehicles, and more. In some cases, I even got to code alongside them, which was a treat. Building on that broad foundation, my work at General Catalyst focuses specifically on data infrastructure that powers AI native apps. It’s an area that I’ve developed so much passion about from firsthand experience building software and working with engineers — I love when I can envision the specific developer I could have unblocked with an infra tool. It is a massive privilege to partner with diverse, ambitious, and brilliant entrepreneurs who I get to learn from every day.
When I’m not working with founders, I can probably be found in one of three places: (1) the soccer field, (2) the ski slopes, or (3) on a plane to a foreign country with far too little luggage.

rows.name: Kelly Carson
lines: I'm senior legal counsel at General Catalyst, an investment and transformation company partnering with leading entrepreneurs to build toward global resiliency and applied AI. At GC, I work with the legal and investment teams to negotiate and close venture capital financings and work with our portfolio companies to assist with their ongoing communications with GC. I'm based in San Francisco.
Prior to joining GC, I was an associate at Goodwin Procter in their technology group, supporting start-ups throughout their life cycle and venture capital funds with their investments.

I graduated from the University of Virginia with a B.A. in English, and later graduated with my J.D. from UC Law San Francisco (formerly UC Hastings). A fun fact about me is that I drove full-sized passenger buses with a commercial driver's license for two years during college.

rows.name: Ken Chenault
lines: At General Catalyst, I am most interested in identifying companies with breakout characteristics, including those that are scaling quickly and have the potential to become significant, global institutions. I also work closely with our portfolio companies, particularly those with an eye towards global markets and responsible innovation, as they scale their teams and products. Companies I’m currently involved with are Bilt Rewards, Chief, CRED, and Guild Education.

I spent 37 years at American Express, most recently as Chairman and CEO, a position I held from 2001 to 2018. I am a co-founder of OneTen, a nonprofit organization of leading companies and CEOs committed to unlocking career opportunities for talent without four-year degrees. I am proud to serve on the boards of Airbnb, Berkshire Hathaway, Chief, Guild Education, and the Harvard Corporation and numerous nonprofit organizations, including the Smithsonian Institution’s Advisory Council for the National Museum of African American History and Culture, the National September 11 Memorial and Museum at the World Trade Center, Bloomberg Philanthropies, the Council on Foreign Relations, and the Human Centered Artificial Intelligence Institute Advisory Council at Stanford University. I also serve on the board of trustees for NYU Langone Health, and as co-chair of Concordance’s First Chance campaign to end the cycle of reincarceration.
I received a BA in history from Bowdoin College and a JD from Harvard Law School. My family and I live in New York City.
rows.title: Chairman & Managing Director

rows.name: Ken Frazier
lines: As Chairman of GC’s Health Assurance Initiatives, I help guide GC’s Health Assurance strategy, which requires building and connecting an extended healthcare ecosystem -- including a closer partnership between healthcare and pharma, and a focus on health equity to ensure quality healthcare is accessible to all. I focus on investments and partnerships, and providing mentorship to founders building companies that are well positioned to transform the healthcare industry through collaborative innovation.

I am also the former executive chairman of the board of directors of Merck, following my retirement from a decade-long tenure as the company’s President and CEO from 2011 to 2021. During my tenure as CEO, Merck delivered innovative lifesaving medicines and vaccines as well as long-term and sustainable value to its multiple stakeholders. I substantially increased Merck’s investment in research, including early research, while refocusing the organization on the launch and growth of key products that provide far-reaching benefits to society. I also led the formation of philanthropic and other initiatives that built on Merck’s 130-year legacy.

As a strong advocate for social justice and economic inclusion, I co-founded and currently serve as co-chair of OneTen, a nonprofit organization of leading companies and CEOs committed to unlocking career opportunities for talent without four-year degrees.

I am proud to serve on the boards of GC portfolio companies Eikon Therapeutics and Paradigm.  I am also on the boards of numerous nonprofit organizations, including the National Constitution Center, Cornerstone Christian Academy in Philadelphia, PA, Weill Cornell Medicine, and the Smithsonian Institution’s Advisory Council for the National Museum of African American History & Culture. I am a member of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences, the American Philosophical Society, The Business Council, the Council of the American Law Institute, the American Bar Association, and a Fellow of the College of Physicians of Philadelphia. Additionally, I am co-chair of the Legal Services Corporation’s Leaders Council.
I received a BA from The Pennsylvania State University and a JD from Harvard Law School.
rows.title: Chairman of Health Assurance Initiatives

rows.name: Ketan Desai
lines: As a Relationship Manager at GC Wealth, I serve as the main point of contact for families, drawing on over two decades of experience in the family office space. My work focuses on navigating their financial journey by providing guidance in the areas of comprehensive cash flow planning across related entities, strategic income and estate wealth planning, philanthropic consulting, and next-gen advisory services.

I hold a CPA license, a Masters in Taxation from Golden Gate University, and an undergraduate degree in Accounting from Southern Methodist University. My wife and I have lived in San Francisco for over 25 years, where we enjoy exploring the Bay Area's diverse culture and cuisines and are proud to have raised our two kids in this incredible city. I also played competitive squash internationally and still enjoy being on the courts occasionally.

rows.name: Kim Baron
lines: I am a Senior Client Service Associate at GC Wealth, a next-generation wealth management platform built for transformational individuals, families, and organizations. It’s a critical component of GC’s effort to go Beyond Venture. At GC Wealth, I serve as a client experience partner for corporate executives, founders, families, and foundations. I take on the role of life administrator and accountability partner for both clients and my team. I collaborate with each family’s trusted advisors to develop a comprehensive and unified strategy to meet their unique needs and goals. I’m based in Bellevue, WA.

Prior to joining GC Wealth, I spent five years as a senior client service associate at UBS and then joined the team at First Republic. With two decades of experience focused on clients' wealth, banking, and lending needs, I specialize in ensuring clients’ needs are promptly met, solving their most complex questions while providing a sense of ease and stability.

I earned a Bachelor of Science in Economics from California State Polytechnic University of Pomona. I’m personally involved with many local charities, including Kindering and The Sibling Support Project.
I enjoy traveling, Tae Kwon Do, and coaching little league with my husband, son, and daughter. After living in Switzerland, I now reside in Kirkland, Washington with my husband, kids, and two hens.

rows.name: KV Mohan
lines: I grew up playing RuneScape. When my parents stopped subsidizing my account, I entertained myself by reading programming textbooks and doing competitive math. Great call by my parents.

I wasn’t cut out for India’s top engineering college, so I came to Stanford to study computer science instead. After college, I started a retail analytics company that was acquired by Palantir. I had to shut down my second company. Building a successful business was hard. Watching one die was harder.

But nothing was harder than spending seven years taking night shifts at San Francisco’s suicide hotline. It gave me a profound appreciation for human psychology and evolved into a lasting obsession with incentive alignment.

Blending my love for math, technology, entrepreneurship, and incentive systems, I founded and co-head the Customer Value Fund (CVF), which I run at General Catalyst. CVF is an entirely new form of financing that my co-head Pranav Singhvi and I created to fund sales and marketing for companies that have found product-market fit. We started at $0 and now manage capital in the ten figures.

I work with unicorns across all sectors, including healthcare (Commure, Ro, Dandy), fintech (Lemonade), enterprise (Factorial, Grammarly), consumer (Fabletics, InDrive), gaming (Superplay), and crypto (to be announced). After all, specialization is for insects.

While there’s nothing more fun than CVF, I’m also into fitness classes, all sports, great food (especially sushi), and great music (especially Metallica). I’m in two book clubs, but still believe the greatest piece of fiction ever created is financial models in Microsoft Excel.
rows.title: Managing Director

rows.name: Larry Bohn
lines: I love building strong companies around great software and helping entrepreneurs scale up their impact, withstand adversity, and achieve something historic. I had the opportunity to build three leading business software companies before joining General Catalyst, taking two of them through their IPOs as CEO.

At General Catalyst, I’m involved with companies that transform a range of industries, including airSlate, B12, Bigcommerce, Black Duck Software (acquired by Synopsys), Clarabridge, Custora, Drift, Feedvisor, GoodData, HubSpot (NYSE: HUBS), Kensho (acquired by S&P Global), Locu (acquired by GoDaddy), Logz.io, L2 (acquired by Gartner), Mark43, OM1, Semantic Machines (acquired by Microsoft), Pelico, PhysicsX, Yottaa, and Zageno.

My path to becoming a venture capitalist is quite unusual; I drove a taxi, worked on a farm, was a short-order cook, and managed a pool hall before getting a BA in English from UMass Amherst and an MA in English Linguistics from Clark University. Later, I taught composition and literature at junior colleges. With an undergrad class in Fortran and some writing skills, I got a job at Data General as a software technical writer and rode the wave that has made software the most important technology of our time.
My investment focus today includes new and existing businesses in cloud-based computing, AI, and SaaS business models, especially with a focus on commerce and analytic applications.

Outside of work, I’m an avid cyclist and occasional woodworker. I’ve been a rider in the Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC) for 22 years and have contributed to raising over $450 million for the Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. I’m also a proud dad (two grown kids working in healthcare) and not a perfect husband married to a near-perfect wife.
rows.title: Managing Director

rows.name: Laura Jacobson
lines: I am a Relationship Manager based in Washington, DC. In my role, I oversee the day-to-day management of client relationships and ensure seamless coordination between our administrative and investment teams. I’m dedicated to delivering an exceptional client experience, built on trust, responsiveness, and attention to detail. I take pride in anticipating client needs, offering proactive guidance, and creating personalized solutions that align with each client’s long-term goals.

My work centers on providing high-net-worth individuals and families with thoughtful support in estate planning, tax optimization, and long-term wealth structuring. I collaborate closely with attorneys and CPA teams to ensure every strategy is executed with precision and care.

Before joining GC Wealth, I was a Client Service Associate at First Republic Bank/J.P. Morgan, where I developed a strong foundation in client relationship management within the private wealth space. I hold a Bachelor of Science in Accounting and Business from Southern New Hampshire University.
I grew up in the White Mountains of New Hampshire, where I developed a passion for hiking, snowboarding, and kayaking—activities I continue to enjoy whenever I can.

rows.name: Laura Yianni
lines: From advising founders on how to tell their stories, to representing General Catalyst across Europe and India - my work spans strategic counsel and hands-on communications, in some of the most complex markets and regulatory environments in the world.

Storytelling is the through-line. What draws me to communications is the hunt for the narrative that makes a strategy legible, a company's purpose felt, or an idea impossible to ignore. I'm endlessly curious about brand story arcs, and what makes something land. I am driven by high standards and a commitment to substantive, high-taste work. Getting the words right is never incidental.

I started at PR consultancy Blue Rubicon (now Teneo), working on multi-sector campaigns for governments, technology and consumer industries. The organization’s mantra - words make history, choose them carefully - has stayed with me.

At Indeed, I spent nearly a decade building the international corporate communications function across 14 markets. As Board Director and Corporate Affairs Board Committee Chair, the work spanned international media, government institutions, and central banks - communications at the level where business strategy and policy collide.

I studied English, Irish & French literature, which set an early obsession with language and how stories work. Outside work: long dog walks, comedy nights, podcasts, and travel - and at home, inventing stories with my two young children, alongside biography and history that explains how we got here.

rows.name: Lee Halloran
lines: I lead Founder Experience at General Catalyst, where I focus on delivering a best-in-class journey for our founders across every touchpoint.

Before GC, I was an operator at Moderna, working on both Brand & Corporate Affairs and Rare Disease. Previously, I spent over 16 years at YouTube and Google in leadership roles across strategy, operations, and partnerships. For much of that time, I led Global Top Creator Strategy & Operations, shaping how YouTube supported its most influential creators and ensuring their needs strategically aligned with YouTube’s product and business priorities. I later helped launch YouTube’s Health initiative, building a health partner ecosystem across multiple countries and partnering with global authorities to define standards for credible health information online.
I began my career at Discovery Networks, driving strategic marketing and revenue growth across its channel portfolio.

I'm passionate about the intersection of technology and public health, and serve on the board of The Mighty Moose, a nonprofit focused on early ovarian cancer detection. I live in Concord, MA with my husband, David, and our three sons — James, Charlie, and Willy. I hold a B.A. from Duke University.

rows.name: Leigh Flor
lines: I am a Wealth Manager at GC Wealth, a next-generation wealth management platform designed for transformational individuals, families, and organizations and a critical component of GC’s mission to go Beyond Venture. At GC Wealth, my passion lies in organizing my clients’ financial lives, so they can focus on what brings them purpose and joy.
Prior to joining GC Wealth, I spent 4 years as Managing Director at First Republic and 15 years at Wells Fargo in roles spanning Private Wealth Management, Banking, and Lending.

I’m committed to supporting non-profit organizations in the Puget Sound, most recently serving on the Board of Directors for Village Theatre. Outside of work, I enjoy traveling, musical theatre, exploring new restaurants, and spending time with my husband and our beloved miniature schnauzer.

rows.name: Lemuel Bourne
lines: I am a client service associate at GC Wealth where I work with clients to provide world-class service as it relates to any administrative and operational needs. I am based in Washington, DC where I coordinate closely with relationship and portfolio managers to ensure our clients feel supported, empowered, and well equipped to plan and execute their financial goals.

Prior to joining GC Wealth, I worked in wealth management as a registered client associate at J.P. Morgan and before that I held the same role at Morgan Stanley. I earned a Bachelors of Business Administration with a concentration in Finance at Loyola University Maryland where I met my wife, Kira. In my free time I enjoy leading an active lifestyle prioritizing health and fitness, as well as volunteering with young people in underserved communities to promote education, financial literacy, and life-skills.

rows.name: Linda Jaeck
lines: Growing up in Germany's automotive heartland with friends and family working in the industry, I developed a deep curiosity for how global political forces shape technological transformation. Witnessing firsthand how major global powers accelerated electrification through regulation and government programs—leaving Germany's industry struggling to adapt—sparked my passion for understanding geopolitical dynamics.

My passion for working at the intersection of innovation and the public good was shaped by hands-on experience across sectors—whether supporting values-based AI regulation at the Aspen Institute, working on digital policy at the European Parliament or identifying tech applications for defense innovation at the Cyber Innovation Hub of the German Armed Forces. These experiences showed me the power of public-private collaboration when it’s purpose-driven and focused on resilience.

My time as a Fellow at General Catalyst was a turning point. I joined a pioneering team helping launch the General Catalyst Institute’s efforts on AI and resilience in Europe. Guided by the belief that startups play a key role in solving today’s policy challenges, I shifted from policy practitioner to ecosystem builder—committed to reducing barriers for mission-driven founders and building bridges between policymakers, investors, and tech leaders.

Now, I focus on the global dialogue on AI while thinking about how Europe can become more competitive, advocating for startup-friendly policy frameworks, and helping create partnerships that support responsible innovation. I bring a mix of strategic insight and a strong grounding in digital governance—combined with interdisciplinary thinking, and a belief that technology should empower, not marginalize, societies.

Outside of work, I co-founded the Hertie Tech Society, where I host events and explore the ethics of emerging tech. I enjoy playing tennis (and most recently padel), love sailing with friends and experimenting with international cuisines in my kitchen.

rows.name: Linda Mauzy
lines: I am a Wealth Manager at GC Wealth, a trusted partner throughout the wealth journey, tailored to the self-made generation, allowing individuals to focus on their company, family, and other life priorities. I am based in Bellevue, Washington.

At GC Wealth, I bring decades of experience spanning Private Wealth Management, having managed funds for institutions, foundations, and individuals at Parametric Portfolio Associates. I approach investment management with a scientific perspective focused on quantitatively driven results, and I hold the Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA) designation.

I bring an intense passion for innovation and for bringing the practical and possible into alignment with clients’ needs. I spend my free time outdoors, hiking and skiing, in addition to serving as a trustee of the Pacific Northwest Research Institute, which focuses on genetics research.

rows.name: Liv Parry
lines: I lead our European Executive Talent initiatives, supporting our portfolio companies with their talent strategies and cultivating key executive networks. Working closely with the founders at the heart of Europe’s entrepreneurial ecosystems, I am deeply passionate about GC’s role in being the epicentre for the next generation of European founders and leaders.

Before joining GC, I was firstminute capital's Head of Portfolio, working across 160 portfolio companies spanning Europe, the US, and some emerging markets. I partnered with early-stage founders at each stage of their companies’ journeys, scaling their teams and helping navigate their bespoke hiring and leadership development challenges. Earlier in my career, I spent time at executive search firms Erevena and Heidrick & Struggles, building leadership teams across both investor-backed tech scale-ups and publicly listed software businesses.

I hold a bachelor’s degree in English Literature with Proficiency in Chinese from the University of Exeter. Off the clock, you can find me on the Padel court, training for a Hyrox, or catching a West End show. Having spent my early years in Hong Kong and Singapore, I’m on a lifelong mission to track down flavours that remind me of home in London.

rows.name: Lloyd W. Brown, II
lines: Vice Chair of Impact Initiatives & Managing Director

My career has been guided by a belief that innovation, institutional capital, and public policy can be powerful forces for expanding economic opportunity and improving lives at scale. Throughout that journey, I have championed a vision of community development that extends beyond affordable housing to include healthcare access, workforce development, educational attainment, financial inclusion, and other drivers of economic mobility.

As Vice Chair & Managing Director for Impact Initiatives at General Catalyst, I advise the firm on regulatory strategy, governance, risk management, and capital deployment initiatives at the intersection of innovation, financial services, and community impact. I provide strategic leadership for the firm’s engagement with regulated financial institutions and the development of scalable investment structures that align commercial objectives with measurable social outcomes. I serve as the firm’s Community Reinvestment Act (CRA) subject matter expert and oversee the development and submission of CRA approval applications to the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC).

Working alongside General Catalyst and other strategic partners, I led the development of the regulatory framework and approval strategy that resulted in multiple first-of-their-kind OCC approvals, including regulatory confirmation that investments in a venture capital-sponsored fund and certain venture-backed operating companies serving low- and moderate-income individuals and communities qualify for CRA consideration. These approvals established new pathways for banks to deploy CRA capital into healthcare, workforce development, and education while maintaining regulatory certainty. This work is expanding the range of eligible CRA activities and demonstrating how venture capital can serve as a catalyst for economic mobility and community impact.

More broadly, these efforts seek to unlock a portion of what is estimated to be more than $1 trillion in annual CRA-related activity generated by approximately 5,000 regulated financial institutions across the United States. As banks grow and their asset bases increase, so do their CRA obligations, creating one of the nation’s largest annually mandated sources of private capital for community and economic development. Within that broader market, CRA-qualified investment activity alone is estimated to exceed $250 billion annually, creating opportunities to direct patient capital toward mission-driven companies capable of delivering both community impact and long-term economic value.

Prior to joining General Catalyst, I founded Brown Management Group, a strategic advisory firm providing regulatory, governance, risk management, and capital formation advice to financial institutions, private equity sponsors, venture capital firms, and growth companies.

With more than three decades of experience spanning banking, law, regulation, compliance, government affairs, and community development, I have held senior leadership positions including Managing Director, Chief Community Reinvestment Act Officer, and Head of the CRA Regulatory Group at Citigroup; Executive Vice President and Head of Government Affairs & Community Development at BNY Mellon; Vice President, Assistant General Counsel, and Deputy Chief Compliance & CRA Officer at IBJ Schroder Bank, a predecessor institution to Mizuho Americas; and Multinational Bank Examiner with the Federal Reserve Bank of New York.

Throughout my career as a Chief CRA Officer, community development executive, and strategic advisor, the institutions and portfolios under my leadership have generated more than $1 trillion in community development loans and investments, demonstrating the transformative potential of private capital to advance economic mobility, strengthen communities, and drive economic revitalization at scale.

Beyond my professional responsibilities, I have served in numerous governance and civic leadership roles, including Chair of The Executive Leadership Council, Chair of New York Mission Society, Chair of Neighborhood Housing Services of New York City, President of the Metropolitan Black Bar Association, Chair of The Bank of New York CRA Grant Committee, Trustee of the BNY Mellon Foundation, and Chair of the Consumer Bankers Association’s Community Reinvestment Committee. I have also served on the boards of the Abyssinian Development Corporation and the Bedford Stuyvesant Restoration Corporation, as well as on the New York City Advisory Board of Local Initiatives Support Corporation.
I earned a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science from Columbia University and a Juris Doctor from Rutgers Law School, and I am admitted to practice law in New York and New Jersey.

The opportunity at General Catalyst brings together the defining themes of my professional journey: innovation, capital formation, regulatory strategy, and community development. It provides a platform to direct capital toward companies and solutions capable of improving health, expanding economic opportunity, strengthening communities, and improving outcomes for millions of people while generating sustainable economic value.
rows.title: Vice Chair of Impact Initiatives & Managing Director

rows.name: Lt. General Scott Howell
lines: I retired from the United States Air Force in August 2021 after a 34-year career during which I held a variety of leadership positions, including most recently as commander of the Joint Special Operations Command (JSOC) at Fort Bragg, North Carolina, from July 2018 to June 2021.

In my role at JSOC, I oversaw military operations across multiple theaters and was responsible for the readiness and mission execution of highly-specialized military forces from the Army, Navy, Air Force, and Marines. Before JSOC, I served as the Vice Commander of U.S. Special Operations Command, focusing on organizing, training, and equipping more than 70,000 U.S. Special Operations personnel operating in more than 85 countries. In this role, I led acquisition, budgeting, programming, and fiscal processes for USSOCOM, working with the military services, Joint Staff, and the Office of the Secretary of Defense.

Previously, I commanded all Coalition special operations forces in Afghanistan as Commanding General of NATO Special Operations Component Command / U.S. Special Operations Joint Task Force – Afghanistan. I have also commanded a squadron, group, joint special operations air component, special operations wing, and a special operations joint task force. My senior staff positions included service in the HQ Air Force Staff, Air Force Special Operations Command, U.S. Special Operations Command, and as the Deputy Director of Special Operations at the Joint Staff. I graduated from the United States Air Force Academy in 1987 and earned Master’s Degrees from the Air Command & Staff College and the National War College.
I am a career helicopter pilot with assignments in rescue and special operations, and I have deployed extensively.
rows.title: Catalyst Advisor

rows.name: Lyman Bullard
lines: I grew up wanting to work in sports. Of course as a kid you think about sports in athletic terms: the game and how it’s played. As an adult, you learn that running a sports team is also a complex financial endeavor with sophisticated investors. So I went to Boston College to study finance, but my internships were somewhat unconventional: Major League Baseball, the Boston Red Sox, and a venture capital firm called General Catalyst.

That last one was really great, but when I graduated I went to work for a minor league hockey team instead. Fortunately, that turned out to be great preparation for coming back to General Catalyst as an analyst. Running a small-market team is a full-court press; you’re interacting with players, owners, competitors and the community. You wear all your hats all the time. I found that to be true of the best investors as well. You have to understand all aspects of business, be able to talk to anyone, and know how to connect the dots.

I moved into Client Solutions & Services with General Catalyst because I love the teamwork it requires and introducing investors to our mission of backing companies that make the world work better. Raising funds in today’s constantly changing landscape of finance and technology is the kind of challenge I enjoy. As in sports, there are always new rules and obstacles in front of you, and you have to embrace them rather than fight them. Then you can turn them into competitive advantages.

While developing my investor relations skills on the job, I also completed my law degree at Suffolk University.  Outside of the office, I am a passionate Boston sports fan, avid golfer, and enjoy getting away to the coast of Maine with my wife and two young sons.

rows.name: Lynn Rueb
lines: I am a Senior Analyst for GC Wealth, specializing in Fixed Income Investments. Based in our San Francisco, CA office, I focus on portfolio management and analysis across all fixed income sectors.

Prior to joining GC Wealth, I dedicated almost 30 years to fixed income trading and management at various Private Wealth institutions, including J.P. Morgan, First Republic Bank, Barclays, and Thomas Weisel Partners.

I hold a BA in Economics and Business from Westmont College in Santa Barbara, CA and a Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA) charterholder.. My youth was spent living and traveling throughout Europe, Asia, and the Middle East, fostering a deep enthusiasm for adventure, learning, and cultural understanding. I currently reside in Danville, CA, where I enjoy spending time with my family and two children.

rows.name: Madhu Namburi
lines: I am a Managing Director at General Catalyst, where I co-lead General Catalyst’s dynamic Creation strategy—championing incubations, transformative ventures, and strategic buyouts. I am also actively involved in late-stage venture investing and in developing new products.

Prior to joining General Catalyst, I spent 25 years at JPMorgan, where I led Global Technology Investment Banking and served on the firm’s Investment Banking Management Committee. Over my career, I've advised on more than 1,000 transactions totaling over $1 trillion, including: Palo Alto Networks’ $25B acquisition of CyberArk, VMware’s $71B sale to Broadcom, Salesforce’s $9B acquisition of Informatica, ServiceNow’s $3B acquisition of Moveworks, Worldpay’s $18.5B sale to GTCR, Silver Lake’s $12.5B acquisition of Qualtrics.

I also led several prominent IPOs, including ZoomInfo, Zoom, HashiCorp, Confluent, Marqeta, Adyen, CrowdStrike, and Cloudflare. In addition, I led JPMorgan’s Tech Venture Investment Fund, where I chaired the Investment Committee, backing next-generation innovators in AI, data analytics, enterprise infrastructure, and disruptive business models.

I live in Hillsborough, CA, with my wife Radhika Mehra, and am the proud father of Ila (20, attending the University of Pennsylvania) and Niam (17). I also serve on the Board of the San Francisco Ballet.
rows.title: Managing Director

rows.name: Marc Bhargava
