lines: At General Catalyst, I lead GC’s Creation strategy, which is focused on incubations as well as transformations and venture buyouts. I also focus on early stage investing across both crypto and fintech, as well as building out the global seed strategy. Additionally, I contribute to GC’s expanding AI efforts.

My core areas of interest include: (1) incubating teams for rolling up services and software businesses and implementing AI transformations to improve profitability and growth; (2) AI meets fintech in spaces such as bookkeeping, accounting, auditing, and insurance; (3) early stage crypto incubation and investing.

Prior to joining GC, I spent years as a founder-operator with an emphasis on new fintech, AI, and crypto technologies. I co-founded Tagomi, one of the first institutional prime brokerages for digital assets (Coinbase purchased Tagomi in 2020), which is now Coinbase Prime.

As an angel investor, I work closely with founders on sales, distribution, and fundraising, investing from my family office in early stage fintech, crypto, and AI/start-up tooling companies. I am an early investor in Ramp, Seel, Zip, Stark Bank, Harvey AI, Codeium, Together AI, Exa, Vantage, Neon, Eigen Layer, Polymarket, Sardine, Doppel, Bridge (acquired by Stripe), DolarApp, Stitch Money, Monad, TRM Labs, and others.
Earlier, I worked at Airbnb, Castanea Partners, and McKinsey, with a focus in business operations and investment analysis.
I received my MBA from Harvard Business School in 2016 and graduated from Harvard College in 2008.
rows.title: Managing Director

rows.name: Marc Harrison M.D.
lines: I am a global healthcare leader, recognized for my work in healthcare transformation and health equity advocacy. I’m a pediatric critical care physician and the former president and CEO of Intermountain Healthcare. I'm currently an advisor at General Catalyst, where previously I joined to launch and lead the Health Assurance Transformation Company (HATCo), a new business owned by GC with the mission to deliver health and wellness collaboratively, compassionately, and courageously—for all people.

As president and CEO of Intermountain, I led the organization to reimagine healthcare operations and champion innovation and collaboration to ensure that our 60,000 caregivers had access to the technology and tools needed to best reach, serve, and empower patients. In my first five years, I executed a disciplined growth strategy with significant investments in telehealth and rural health, expanding Intermountain’s service area from primarily Utah communities to serving patients throughout the Mountain West.

Under my leadership, Intermountain embraced unconventional, public-private partnerships to tackle some of the most pressing systemic challenges facing communities and the industry. We proactively worked to keep people well and make communities healthier. These initiatives helped catalyze the national movement toward value-based care, advance clinical education, and establish a new Digital Hippocratic Oath—developed by Graphite, a company co-founded by Intermountain—to improve hospital data interoperability and secure patient privacy rights.

During my tenure, we partnered with over 1,000 hospitals nationwide to launch Civica Rx, a nonprofit generic drug manufacturer and distributor, aimed at making generic medications—like insulin, which we plan to offer in 2024—more accessible and affordable. We were also a founding member of the Utah Alliance for the Determinants of Health, a collaboration of community partners focused on addressing the forces that affect people's ability to stay healthy. Additionally, we partnered with an international genomics leader and over 100,000 volunteers to advance medical breakthroughs to help prevent and treat genetic diseases globally.

Before leading Intermountain, I served as CEO of Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi, chief of international business development at Cleveland Clinic, and chief medical operations officer at Cleveland Clinic. Fortune recognized me as one of the Top 50 World’s Greatest Leaders in 2019, and Modern Healthcare has consistently named me among the Most Influential People in Healthcare. I’m also the author of Possibility Unleashed: Pathbreaking Lessons for Making Change Happen in Your Organization and Beyond, a guide for leaders on overcoming fear, transcending discord and polarization, and driving positive systemic and societal change.

I received my undergraduate degree from Haverford College and my medical degree from Dartmouth Medical School. I completed a pediatric residency and pediatric critical care fellowship at Intermountain’s Primary Children’s Hospital, and earned a Master of Medical Management from Carnegie Mellon University.

I’m an all-American triathlete and represented the U.S. at the 2014 World Championships. I’m also a two-time cancer survivor and nine-time Ironman participant. Above all, I’m a loving husband and proud father of three adult children.

rows.name: Mark Allen
lines: My first experience of General Catalyst came when I worked at PwC. At that time, General Catalyst was just a year old. More than a decade later, I was reunited with the General Catalyst team when I joined them to manage the financial accounting, reporting and treasury functions. We’ve all grown a bit, but the spirit, energy and values that helped form General Catalyst are as vital as ever.

One of the best things about working with General Catalyst is the rich interaction across the various teams and among the highly varied individuals. On a daily basis, those of us in finance and operations work directly with the investment team to help support them and their entrepreneurs in many aspects of the business.

One of my roles is to utilize technology to increase efficiency – something many of our entrepreneurs are doing with their visionary businesses. We’re always looking for ways to streamline operations so our investment team has more time for our entrepreneurs and their companies. That makes this part of my job truly mission-driven, which only adds to how much I enjoy it.

I am a true New Englander, raised and educated in Vermont, and later attended Northeastern University for my MBA. I’m still able to beat my three young daughters down the ski slopes, and I enjoy a round of golf on the weekend.
rows.title: Head of Equity Fund Finance

rows.name: Mark Crane
lines: I acquired my respect for entrepreneurs through my own journey as a founder. As a freshman at Amherst, I jumped at the opportunity to operate my own business, providing summer and year-round storage solutions for students at Amherst College, UMASS, Mt. Holyoke, Smith, and Hampshire. It was a formative experience -- hiring, staying ahead of the competition and making the numbers. When I graduated, I sought out a role in finance to gain a deeper understanding of the underlying metrics that make a business successful.

Working closely with investors and entrepreneurs at JMI and Cove Hill showed me how complex and wonderful those roles and relationships could be. Companies are living, breathing organisms, and founders are the forces of nature that drive them. The best investors are endlessly curious; they not only want to learn from previous experiences, but they also want to discover entirely new ways to support the success of a team and company.

The drive to help identify and collaborate with impactful founders across the technology ecosystem is what ultimately led me to General Catalyst. I am most excited about working with the team to help unlock the knowledge and expertise across the General Catalyst network.

My passion away from work is soccer. I captained the men’s team at Amherst and still love the game, whether it’s watching matches or getting onto the field on weekends. Although a little slower than I was, I enjoy the competition and being part of a team. Outside of the pitch, you can find me finding a good weekend trip.

rows.name: Maryam Mujica
lines: I currently serve as the President of the General Catalyst Institute (GCI), where I lead a global team working at the intersection of venture capital and government to strengthen national resilience through transformative technologies.

Over the last two decades, my career has spanned the worlds of law, government, and the technology sector. I began practicing law before entering public service, where I focused on some of the United States' most complex geopolitical challenges. While serving at the U.S. Department of State and later on The White House National Security Council, I witnessed firsthand during the Arab Spring how technology was reshaping societies and geopolitics across the Middle East in real time.

That experience inspired my transition to the private sector, where I have helped some of the world's leading technology companies navigate challenging and ever-evolving policy and regulatory environments. I led all Executive Branch engagement for Twitter before leading Emerging Markets for Google's International Government Affairs team. I later built Shopify's global government affairs function and subsequently led public affairs across the Americas for Booking Holdings and its portfolio of brands, including Booking.com, Kayak, Priceline, and Agoda.

I earned my bachelor's degree from Trinity College, J.D. from Santa Clara University School of Law, and a Master's Certificate in Public Administration from the University of Virginia. I am licensed to practice law in California, speak Spanish, and am conversant in French and Farsi. I live in Washington, D.C., with my husband and daughter.
rows.title: President, GCI

rows.name: Maryam Sabour
lines: I'm VP of Partnerships at General Catalyst, where I lead the firm's partnership strategy across its $40+ billion in AUM. I pursue strategic partnerships that drive exponential growth across GC, accelerating portfolio companies through differentiated opportunities while propelling GC's transformation initiatives, products and services through innovative collaborations. I'm based in San Francisco.

Previously, I was Head of Business Development at Niantic, where I led strategic partnerships across the company's augmented reality platform and global games portfolio (e.g. Pokémon GO). I spearheaded Niantic's expansion into spatial computing as General Manager for AR Hardware, forging landmark partnerships with Snap, Meta, and Qualcomm. I have deep expertise building businesses leveraging computer vision and Physical AI, including the development of the industry's first Large Geospatial Model for machines navigating real-world environments. Before Niantic, I was a strategy consultant advising early-stage AR/VR/AI companies in the advertising, film, and entertainment verticals.

I'm a licensed attorney holding a J.D. and Bachelor of Civil Law from McGill University, and a Bachelor of Commerce with distinction from Toronto Metropolitan University. I co-founded Compass Startup & Legal Clinic to democratize legal services for underserved entrepreneurs, where I continue to serve as Chair of the Board. I also established McGill University's Silicon Valley presence, creating the institution's first West Coast program for the Dobson Centre for Entrepreneurship, which has incubated over 500 startups and raised over $4 billion in funding. I'm a builder at heart and believe that technology should be used to bring people closer together.

rows.name: Matt Hollinshead
lines: I am a Director in the Human Resources team at General Catalyst, a global investment and transformation company that partners with the world’s most ambitious entrepreneurs to drive resilience and applied AI. I’m based in London, focusing on all things HR for our London, Berlin and Bangalore offices.

Before joining GC I worked in a HR generalist capacity for a Canadian pension fund based in London, but looking after colleagues across Europe, India and Singapore. Prior to this I worked in the resourcing team for a European investment bank.

I recently became a father, so most of my time outside of the office is currently spent trying to figure out how to parent! When I’m not doing that, I can be found at a restaurant with my wife or socialising with friends, or on the golf course.

rows.name: Max Rimpel
lines: Having grown up in a small village in Germany, I have a deep appreciation for entrepreneurship. To this day, I believe it’s the most powerful mechanism to bring about positive change. My drive “to see the world” ultimately led me to high school in the U.S., university in Berlin, advanced degrees in Paris and Madrid, internships in Japan and Brazil, stints at intergovernmental institutions and equity market research in the U.S. I was intrigued how technology changed our lives and began my tech career at Google in London.

I transitioned into venture capital, joining Index Ventures, just as Europe became a fertile ground for ambitious founders. At General Catalyst, I continue to focus on B2B investment opportunities, now across both New York and Europe, which are the two ecosystems I’m most bullish about. Away from work, I love any sport involving a racquet or paddle, am a passionate piano player of limited ability and support organisations that take on big challenges, such as Human Rights Watch and Black Girls CODE.

rows.name: Maya Andrews
lines: When I graduated from Stanford with a degree in management science and engineering, I already had a job offer – but I delayed the start of my career to compete in the 2016 Olympics, where I won two gold medals as part of the U.S. swim team. While I could have won more races, I was eager to join the team at McKinsey & Company.

I later moved into the social sector to invest philanthropic capital toward high-performing organizations working to alleviate extreme poverty in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia. Having learned that innovative businesses can play a major role in effecting social change alongside the public sector, I returned to Stanford for an MBA. As I note, societal expectations for the private sector are rising, and a new generation of investors and founders can take that challenge in powerful new directions.

I came to General Catalyst to expand and enhance the firm’s capacity for stewarding invested funds that empower mission-driven businesses. As someone who thrives on understanding and communicating with investors, I seek to build relationships that last decades.

Away from the office, I enjoy raising a family, cooking complex recipes from scratch, and romping with my Bernedoodle. Still an athlete at heart, I remain connected to my sport by serving on the board of USA Swimming, but I’ve now picked up running and cycling as well – there may be a triathlon in my future.

rows.name: Micah Karson
lines: At General Catalyst, I focus on building investor relationships and driving capital formation across our fund products.

Before joining General Catalyst, I spent seven years at Partners Group in client solutions, where I developed a passion for private markets fundraising. Prior to that, I worked at Bloomberg LP as an enterprise relationship manager.
I hold a bachelor's degree in public policy from the University of Michigan and an MBA from Columbia Business School.
Outside of work, you can find me in a hot yoga class or spending time in Central Park with my wife and daughter.

rows.name: Michael Kato
lines: Head of Financial Planning, GC Wealth

I am Head of Financial Planning at GC Wealth, where I advise clients across all aspects of the planning experience, with a particular focus on income, gift, and estate tax planning. I work closely with start-up founders and their teams in all areas of personal finance and taxation throughout their journey of wealth creation and stewardship. I also partner with companies developing fintech solutions that are shaping and enabling the transformation of the wealth management industry.

Before GC, I was Managing Director of Advanced Planning at First Republic Bank and a Senior Wealth Planning Strategist and Regional Wealth Planning Manager at Wells Fargo in Palo Alto. I began my career in Tokyo as an international tax director, advising individuals and corporations on cross-border tax issues.

I graduated from the University of California, Los Angeles with a Bachelor’s in Japanese and a specialization in Business Administration. I also received a Master's in Financial Planning from Golden Gate University, where I studied Personal Finance and Tax.

In my free time, I enjoy cycling for fun and fitness. I lead a weekly interval training ride through Los Altos Hills every Tuesday evening. I am committed to bicycle safety and serve as my son’s school representative on the Palo Alto City/School Transportation Safety Committee (CSTSC), where I advocate for bicycle and pedestrian safety for young students traveling to school on city streets.
rows.title: Head of Financial Planning, GC Wealth

rows.name: Mike Bolner
lines: I am a member of the investor relations team at General Catalyst, specializing in product development. As an investment banker, I previously worked with General Catalyst as a client since 2020. After a five-year audition, it is exciting to now be part of the firm based in New York.

Previously, I was an investment banker since 1997 raising capital for alternative investment firms. Since 2018, I was a Partner at Campbell Lutyens, the largest global placement agent that over the past few years has raised the most institutional capital in the placement industry. Before that, I was at Citi and JPMorgan. Over the past 25 years, I have led over 85 fundraises for venture capital, private equity, real assets and credit funds. I got into the fundraising profession as alternatives were just becoming a mainstream asset class.  During this time, investors have grown their alternatives portfolios dramatically although fundraising has never been easy.  I am thrilled to join General Catalyst, a firm that has enjoyed great fundraising success given its strong brand, talented team and successful track record.

I graduated from Penn State with a finance degree and have an MBA from Harvard Business School. I grew up in Pittsburgh, PA and am an avid Steelers and Penn State sports fan.  After 25+ years in New York, I have become a big fan of the Knicks but no other New York sports teams.  I struggle to keep up with my fitness and enjoy walking around NYC.  My wife, dog (havanese) and I live on the Upper West Side and we have two grown daughters, ages 25 and 23.

rows.name: Molly Gillis
lines: I am a Partner and Chief of Staff at global investment and transformation company General Catalyst. I have more than 25 years of experience in VC and tech, focused on communications, operations, and relationship building.

In my current role, I guide the company’s communications strategy and execution, collaborating with a global team to create successful outcomes for GC and its portfolio. I also partner with GC’s chairman Ken Chenault and GC’s chairman of health assurance initiatives Ken Frazier on their executive communications, and their work with GC portfolio companies, the external organizations with which they are affiliated, and mission-driven initiatives that are in service of making a positive impact on society.

Having joined GC at its formation, I was responsible for establishing its investor relations, marketing, PR, and internal communications functions in partnership with its founders, and played a leadership role in creating opportunities to build GC’s brand and ecosystem through strategic partnerships, media relations, creative events, and new initiatives.

Throughout my career, I have held leadership positions spanning  marketing, communications, operations, business development and strategy at Leerink Partners, a healthcare investment bank, Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, and BBN Technologies (a GC portfolio company acquired by Raytheon).
I am a writer and an active member of my community. I earned a B.A. in English from Mount Saint Mary’s University and an M.A. in publishing at Emerson College.

rows.name: Nat Levy-Westhead
lines: I learned early in life that my natural love of making connections became even more interesting when I understood complex topics from the inside. At Brown University, I pursued simultaneous degrees in computer science and economics so I could grasp how digital innovation arises from the marriage of business and technology. After that, I joined a boutique investment banking firm, where I worked on deals involving Pandora, TiVO, and Shutterfly.

I then pivoted into operations with Plaid, a fintech infrastructure startup, to learn how new products are inspired, created, developed, and brought to market. There, I worked on developing a capital allocation strategy, evaluating M&A opportunities, and raising capital to fund the company’s growth. As I’ve come to realize, it’s hard to understand just how difficult it is to scale a company until you do it – and people are by far the most critical factor for success.

Now, with General Catalyst, I’m part of the fintech team, exploring how digitizing money can increase efficiency for SMBs, help modernize emerging economies, and unleash entrepreneurial energy across industries. I believe that all fintech companies will face tremendous change in the coming years, and the winners will be those who create the most value for all stakeholders in their ecosystems.
Outside the office, I’ve become an avid pickleball player, but when I’m not on the court, I enjoy hiking or relaxing with a good book or movie.

rows.name: Neeraj Arora
lines: I am the founder of Venture Highway, which I established before joining forces with General Catalyst as Managing Director. Venture Highway has backed companies such as Meesho, Sharechat, Moglix, and MPL at their earliest stages.

Before my current role, I was the Global Head of Business at WhatsApp, where I led WhatsApp’s $19B sale to Facebook in 2014. Prior to my time at WhatsApp, I served as Principal of Corporate Development at Google. I also serve as a Board Member of the UCSF Foundation and the IIT Delhi Endowment Fund.
I hold a degree in Mechanical Engineering from the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), New Delhi, and a Master’s in Business Administration from the Indian School of Business.
Seeding the Future with Vital Lyfe
rows.title: CEO India, MENA & Managing Director

rows.name: Nichole Heidrick
lines: I am a Wealth Manager at GC Wealth, a next-generation wealth management platform built for transformational individuals, families, and organizations, and a critical component of GC’s endeavor to go Beyond Venture. I have served clients for over two decades, previously at Goldman Sachs, Wells Fargo Private Bank, and First Republic. I bring to my work an open and curious mind and a commitment to co-creating alongside clients with great caring and integrity.
I graduated with a BA in History from the University of Virginia and received my MBA in Finance and Accounting from the NYU Stern School of Business.

When I'm not working to catalyze the wealth management industry, I can be found coaching women on career, life, and wealth issues; volunteering for causes related to girls and education (I’m a board member of the Rwanda Girls Initiative); in a CrossFit gym (I’m a Level I certified coach); or spending time with my fiancée raising our 5 teenage children in Bellevue, WA.

rows.name: Nick Cohen
lines: As Director of Global Content and Editorial at General Catalyst, I shape the company's content strategy and thought leadership.

Prior to joining GC, I led the International Strategy Forum, a global fellowship program founded by ex-Google CEO Eric Schmidt that bridges the worlds of technology and geopolitics. I have overseen strategic communications for multinational programs including the Quad Fellowship, collaborated with world-renowned journalist Fareed Zakaria on his book Age of Revolutions, and worked on state and congressional electoral campaigns in my home state of Minnesota.

A historian of modern Central and Eastern Europe by training, I earned degrees at Columbia University and Carleton College. My work has been published in Foreign Policy, New Eastern Europe, and the Journal of International Affairs. I am also the lead editor of European Integration and Disintegration, published by Routledge.

Outside of work, you can find me reading (mostly history, although I'm branching out into more fiction), traveling (35 countries and counting), enjoying the Brooklyn Botanic Garden, playing squash, and exploring the Upper West Side (the best neighborhood in NYC).

rows.name: Otto Salmi
lines: I grew up in a family of tinkerers who taught me to appreciate the craftsmanship and effort behind the everyday machines and systems around us. This shaped my belief that our hardest problems can be solved by people who break them down to first principles, think across disciplines, and aren't afraid to build something new.

At General Catalyst, I partner with founders building in critical industries, spanning energy, industrials, aerospace and beyond. Through our Global Resilience practice, I help companies match the right capital for their unique growth trajectory across our Venture and Creation strategies as well as our Customer Value Fund.

From my first job on the floor of a metal shop, I became a mechanical engineer at SpaceX, designing propulsion systems for launch vehicles, and later moved to Tesla, working in battery engineering and strategic finance. I graduated magna cum laude from Dartmouth, where I studied mechanical engineering and economics and led our local mountain's ski patrol unit. I later earned my MBA with distinction from Harvard Business School. Outside of work, you'll find me surfing, biking, skiing, or exploring the California coast with my wife.

rows.name: Paul Fielding
lines: My career has not been a straight line, however, I realize now that both my academic career and my business experience were all in preparation for the opportunity that lies ahead of me today. I studied economics at UCLA while also working full-time in mortgage analytics, with all its wonderfully complicated, data-driven problems; then co-founding a company and scaling it through the usual life-or-death situations entrepreneurs face on their way to their first $1 million in revenue; and finally, coming to General Catalyst to work with early-stage companies and providing them with a wider range of financing options.

My reward for all that preparation is the opportunity to head operations at General Catalyst during an inflection point in the firm’s evolution from a successful partnership to an enduring global enterprise that serves CEOs at every stage of their companies’ development. In my role, I work closely with the firm’s leadership, our investment team, our entrepreneurs, and our limited partners, while keeping the firm’s internal infrastructure evolving to meet our ambitions.

When I leave the office, I like to head for the kitchen or the grill, where I can indulge my love of cooking and invite friends and family to share the results. I’m also an avid reader of history, because knowing where we’ve been can help us understand where we’re going as individuals, teams, and as a part of the global economy.
rows.title: Chief Financial Officer

rows.name: Paul Kwan
lines: My parents came to America from Hong Kong in the late 1960s after the passage of the Immigration and Nationality Act of 1965, which ended de facto discrimination against immigrants from Southern Europe, Eastern Europe, and Asia. My father became a professor of astrophysics at UMass-Amherst, which is where I grew up. My mother and her two sisters became computer programmers after college in the 1970s, and my mother worked as a programmer for over 30 years. Her appreciation for tech is what led me to study computer science at Stanford.

I started my career on Wall Street just as the Internet we know today was taking shape. A few years later, I had the opportunity to join Morgan Stanley’s Menlo Park office, where I thrived for 22 years, including six years running the bank’s global internet and software business and six years leading the West Coast team. That continuity became a great asset because it took time to learn the craft of advising companies on their most important strategic and financial objectives. It also allowed me to see firsthand what world-class tech companies do to create enduring value, whether it was strategic, financial, operational, or cultural.

At GC, I lead the Global Resilience team, which focuses on modernizing our most critical societal systems, including defense and intelligence, industrial, and energy sectors. I look for mission-driven, software-enabled companies that are category-defining in their own unique way. I'm the co-founder of Valinor, a modern defense tech holding company. I've led investments in Anduril, Castelion, Charm Industrial, Helsing, Nominal, Onebrief, PhysicsX, Re:Build, Samsara, Saronic, and Substrate.

I’m an adjunct lecturer at Stanford and, for many years, I taught a class at the Haas School of Business on tech IPOs and M&A. My wife and I are supporters of pioneering neuropsychiatric research at Stanford University's Pasca Lab to better understand autism, psychiatric disorders, and orphan genetic diseases like 22q11. I also serve as vice chair of the Lucille Packard Foundation for Children's Health.
rows.title: Managing Director

rows.name: Paul Sagan
lines: I am an internet technology entrepreneur and award-winning former journalist, and now I advise internet software, services, and infrastructure CEOs and their teams on strategy and execution as a Catalyst Advisor. I primarily work as a board member of public and private companies, and I was previously a Managing Director at General Catalyst.

I currently sit on the boards of five GC portfolio companies (airSlate, Bugcrowd, Casana, Section, and Zorus). Previously, as a Managing Director and advisor to the firm, I served as Non-Executive Chairman of Datto (acquired by Vista Equity Partners), Non-Executive Chairman of L2 (acquired by Gartner), and as a director of Anaconda (acquired by Morningside).

I'm also a director of Moderna (NASDAQ: MRNA) and was the lead independent director of VMware until the company’s sale to Broadcom in 2023. Earlier in my career, I served as a director of iRobot (NASDAQ: IRBT) and as a board member of Dow Jones & Company, Digitas, EMC, and Maven Networks before they were acquired.

I worked at Akamai Technologies (NASDAQ: AKAM), joining as Chief Operating Officer and employee #15 in 1998 when the company launched out of MIT. Later, I served as President and then as CEO for nine years until 2013. I was a member of Akamai’s board of directors until 2019. My work at Akamai earned me the title of 2009 EY Technology Entrepreneur of the Year.

I began my career in broadcast television news, joining WCBS-TV in 1981 as a news writer and eventually becoming news director. I won three Emmy Awards for TV news in New York City. I also held senior management roles at Time Warner, where I helped found RoadRunner, the world’s first consumer broadband service; Pathfinder, one of the first web portals that pioneered internet advertising; and NY 1, the 24-hour cable news channel.

Today, I also serve as Chairman of the Board of ProPublica, the not-for-profit investigative journalism organization, and as a trustee of the Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center of Boston. I am a Fellow of the American Academy of Arts & Sciences and previously served as a member of the MIT Visiting Committee in the Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science. In terms of public service, I was Chair of the Massachusetts Board of Elementary and Secondary Education from 2015 to 2019 under an appointment by Governor Baker, and I was a member of the National Security Telecommunications Advisory Committee (NSTAC) from 2010 to 2017 under an appointment by President Obama.
I am a graduate of Northwestern University, where I am a life trustee.
rows.title: Catalyst Advisor

rows.name: Peter Njuguna
lines: As a member of the Compliance team at GC Wealth, I focus on developing and enhancing a risk-based compliance program tailored to the firm’s unique business model and clients. Our goal is to build scalable frameworks that effectively identify, monitor, and mitigate regulatory and operational risks while supporting business growth and innovation.

Before joining GC Wealth, I served as a Compliance Examiner at the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), where I led regulatory examinations of investment advisers and private fund managers. In that role, I gained deep experience assessing firms’ compliance programs, governance structures, and adherence to federal securities laws.
Earlier in my career, I worked in compliance at a hedge fund manager in Boston, where I supported day-to-day regulatory functions, testing, and internal control reviews across trading and operations.
Outside of work, I enjoy spending time with my wife and puppy, watching and playing tennis, reading, and following English Premier League football (Chelsea) and Formula 1 racing.

rows.name: Peter Nonis
lines: I serve as the Vice President of Policy Communications and Programs at the General Catalyst Institute (GCI) where I work to accelerate effective global public policies that enable the growth and scale-up of startups. This is achieved by engaging the institute with key stakeholders on solutions vital to strengthening national resilience around the world through transformative technologies.

Prior to my current role, I led marketing and communications for a leading global business council, partnering with the public and private sectors to expand international trade and commerce. My time there allowed me to work with a dynamic array of world leaders, ranging from global CEOs and sovereign wealth funds, to heads of state and broadcast journalists.

Earlier in my career, I was engaged in public affairs efforts for numerous trade associations in support of increased infrastructure investment, prioritizing safety and resilience, and boosting competitiveness, while serving as an on-the-record spokesperson on myriad policy issues.

I received my BA in Political Science from American University in Washington, DC, and reside in Fairfax, Virginia with my two daughters. When I'm not busy focused on politics and policy, you can find me at the nearest body of water fishing for whatever bites.

rows.name: Phillip Riese
lines: Through Riese & Others, my focus is on providing strategic consulting, board, and advisory services to enterprises globally, with a particular passion for growth companies, primarily those disrupting the financial services industry.

I bring almost 30 years of executive and operating experience to the table, combined with an additional 20 years of working with some of the most innovative, disruptive, rapidly growing, and successful startup and growth companies and their management teams around the world.

Over the last 20 years, I have served on a number of public and private company boards, and today I am a board member of public companies: Flywire (FLYW) and Remitly (RELY), and private companies: Array, Betterment, Cross River, Mpower, Perch, and Relay Network. I am an adviser to a number of private company CEOs and venture funds globally. I also serve as a board member of Accion, a not-for-profit dedicated to global financial inclusion.

Prior to the formation of RIESE & OTHERS, I spent 18 years at American Express in a variety of positions, and for the last 8 years, I served as the president of the Consumer Card Group and chairman of American Express Centurion Bank. Before American Express, I had been a division executive at Chase Manhattan Bank, responsible for their Merchant Services business, and a partner of M.C. Geffen and Associates, a consulting firm in South Africa.

I am a Textile Engineer, earning a bachelor’s degree in Commerce from Leeds University in England, an MBA from the University of Cape Town in South Africa, and a Master of Science degree from MIT's Sloan School of Management.
My wife Tracey and I live in Brooklyn, New York.
rows.title: Catalyst Advisor

rows.name: Pranav Singhvi
lines: Growing up in Abu Dhabi, I enjoyed physics but became fascinated by capital markets when I experienced the inauguration of the country’s first stock market. The impact it had on the region is hard to overstate and I’ve been in the quest of understanding how markets work ever since. My love for physics led me to study mechanical engineering at the University of Illinois, but I dabbled in equity markets throughout college. While engineering was fun, I decided to go in a different direction after graduation. I instead spent time learning about how businesses make capital allocation decisions, which led me to consulting first and then to investment banking.

During my time in those roles, it became clear to me that most businesses were not yet sophisticated when it came to augmenting their instincts with data. The same core issue persisted: the lack of clean integrated data. Of the work I did, the tools that I built to help with data integration had the biggest impact on the economics of the projects I worked on. It became clear to me that there was a massive opportunity in data integration, and that led me to the data integration company Palantir Technologies. At Palantir, I ran the Strategic Finance team where we built a systematic approach in allocating our resources to optimize top line growth, drive the unit economics of the business and quarterback our fundraising. It was an incredible experience, as I was able to tie everything I’d learned about capital allocation and human-computer augmentation together.
After five years at Palantir,  I was ready for my next challenge and joined GC, where I’m focused on applying what I’ve learned so far to private capital markets.
On weekends, I can be found playing cricket at one of the baseball fields in San Francisco or lurking on Twitter to find the highest quality pseudonymous accounts.
rows.title: Managing Director

rows.name: Quentin Clark
lines: People who know me from my roles at Dropbox, SAP, and Microsoft might think of me as a product and strategy leader, but I started coding as a kid and came up as a software engineer. I am curious about technology and how it can empower building and problem solving. When I had a “gap year” between my last two enterprise jobs, I embraced the opportunity to get closer to the roots of the entrepreneurial world as a board member, advisor, and angel investor. This lead me to starting a career in venture capital.

I joined General Catalyst to be more of a force multiplier by sharing what I’ve learned with more founders and leaders than I could inside any one company. The company is home to successful operators and systems thinkers who aim to reshape industries and society.  My core areas of focus as an investor are on transformative infrastructure and products that empower every day work.  At GC, I work in early AI and enterprise infrastructure investing and led our investments in MinIO, Eightfold, Glean, Neon, Metronome, Codeium, DataVolo, and others.

I earned degrees in Physics and Computer Science from the University of Massachusetts at Amherst and continue to support the university, including through a scholarship for students pursuing multi-disciplinary studies. Outside of work, I enjoy spending time with family and friends, cooking, exploring wine, watching movies, and taking care of my Australian Shepherds.
rows.title: Managing Director

rows.name: Quincy Darbyshire
lines: At General Catalyst, I focus on helping our portfolio companies thrive — connecting founders and their teams with the rapidly expanding GC platform and ensuring they have the information, tools, and relationships to drive transformation in their respective industries.

Prior to GC, I dedicated myself to building systems that help companies and people grow — from early-stage startups like fullcast, where I was an early employee building the next generation of RevOps software, to larger organizations like Salesforce during its high-growth years, where I helped guide GTM strategy in AMER, LATAM, and APAC. I have also served as an executive coach working closely with founders and their teams in a variety of situations.

My range of work experience has shaped empathy for the challenges that founders and their companies face at every stage, and an understanding of how the right support and systems can make all the difference. I feel incredibly fortunate to be in a position to leverage GC’s platform and resources to help make that difference.

Originally from Savannah, Georgia — the “Hostess City of the South” — I believe strongly in the importance of hospitality and service and in the strength of community. I am also a competitive rower, and strive to work with our portfolio companies the same way I do on the water: team-first, in-sync, and seeing how fast we can go together.
I am based in San Francisco with my wife and young daughter, and am a proud alum of Dartmouth College and The Wharton School.

rows.name: Rachit Neupane
lines: I am an investor at General Catalyst, where I contribute to the health assurance team by driving success for the firm’s portfolio companies and new investments across biotech and life sciences.

Before joining GC, I was an investor at CaaS Capital Management, where I helped establish the firm’s biotech strategy for private and public markets. Prior to CaaS, I began my career as a consultant at Clarion, a biopharma consultancy firm.
I earned a BS in biology at Bard College, a healthcare certificate at Sloan School of Management, and my PhD in biology at MIT.

rows.name: Rahul Garg
lines: I am an entrepreneur turned investor currently at General Catalyst - India, a venture capital firm that partners with founders from seed through growth stages and beyond to build companies that withstand the test of time. At GC, I focus on investment opportunities in India.

Prior to joining GC, I spent over a decade in the India tech ecosystem, initially as a founder, and later, as a VC with premier investment firms like Kalaari Capital and Venture Highway. I have investment experience across stages (early + growth) and across sectors (B2C, B2B, SAAS).

As an entrepreneur, I built two e-commerce companies in India for 5 years. My first startup, Artisangilt.com, focused on consolidating the ethnic wear and fashion jewelry markets in India, and was acquired by IGP.com in 2014, after which I moved to IGP as the CEO of the company. IGP is currently the largest online gifting company in India. At both Artisangilt & IGP, I was directly responsible for product, strategy, and marketing.
In my early days, I spent 8 years in capital markets as a sell-side Equity Research Analyst covering mid-to-large cap stocks in the UK/Europe at Lehman Brothers, and then in India at HSBC Securities.
I am an IIT Bombay alum and a CFA charter holder.

rows.name: Rahul Humayun
lines: At General Catalyst, I invest in India-first consumer tech and fintech companies. I most love products and business models that counter position, are disruptive, and sometimes outright weird! This reflects my belief that innovation always starts at the edges, in the most unexpected places.

Prior to joining GC, I was an early-stage investor at Elevation Capital where I looked at investments in fintech and gaming. At Elevation, I was involved in seven new investments and have had the privilege of working with founders across stages. Before that I was at Nomura where I was part of the strategy team, working on projects related to Digital Asset Strategy (helped set up Nomura's crypto entity Laser Digital), Business Optimisation and Capital Markets restructuring.
I graduated from the Indian Institute of Technology Madras with a B.Tech in Chemical Engineering. I was an avid quizzer, powerlifter and an elected representative in college.
When not meeting with founders or typing away at my desk, you’ll find me at the gym, bumping the newest Drake song, gaming or bingeing on history documentaries.

rows.name: Rashmi Shivashankar
lines: As a child, my favorite part of the day was going to work with my dad and pretending to be a manager at his office. I was paid a dollar for every call I made to collect dues owed to him. I soon started doing anything creative that would make me money (like getting printouts for my older neighbors, running a used book library as a 10-year-old, letting kids borrow my Nintendo for a small cost). That early experience probably laid the foundation for my eventual career in venture capital law.

I started my legal career in Bangalore, India and National University of Singapore (I also studied for a bit in Shanghai, China), joining top-tier firms like Amarchand and AZB as a corporate attorney in India. I came across an opportunity at Sequoia Capital India (now Peak XV Partners) and worked there for over 7 years in the venture capital world as a lawyer, before moving to General Catalyst to head their legal operations in India. I absolutely love what I do—negotiating documents and helping founders navigate difficult regulatory problems.

On the personal front, I love my family, sports—Padel being my current favorite—and indie music (I make Sunday playlists on Spotify). I also played cricket at the national level for India 'A'. I'm always on the hunt for good restaurants in any new place I travel to. I have an adorable toy poodle called 'Gatsby' who is the absolute love of my life.

rows.name: Reggie James
lines: I'm the Creative Director at General Catalyst, a transformation company that is engineering resilience to tackle some of the world's toughest problems. At GC, I shape our brand, storytelling, and design. Not just for GC the firm, but for our portfolio companies, founders, partners, and transformation companies.

Prior to joining GC, I was the co-founder and ceo of Eternal. An AI gaming and new media company that was acquired in 2025. We were fortunate enough to release a number of products and experiences that connected across technology and culture. Collaborating with artists and cultural figures like Heron Preston, Gus Dapperton, Julia Fox, New York Fashion Week, Geese, and many more.

I graduated from Wharton at the University of Pennsylvania with a BS in Economics. My individualized concentration centered on a question I still ask in my writing today, why do we design the things we design - and why does capital seem to love some ideas and not others. It was this thesis that allowed me to fall in love with writing, which has continued for several years on my Substack Product Lost.

One fun fact about me is that I had the honor of launching Rough Draft Penn, GC's previous student investment effort. So in many ways joining GC has been a full circle moment to a family that gave me so much.
rows.title: Creative Director

rows.name: Reva Nohria
lines: I am a Partner on the Health Assurance team at General Catalyst, working with founders to create a more proactive, affordable, and equitable system of care. I studied the History of Art & Architecture, developing a multidisciplinary approach to understanding people and ideas, drawing from sociology, anthropology, philosophy, and economics.

My career began at Disney's Corporate Strategy & Business Development group, where I contributed to the conceptualization of Disney+ and the acquisition of 21st Century Fox. Watching Disney reinvent itself through technology ignited my interest in entrepreneurship and venture capital.

Since joining General Catalyst in 2018, I have focused on healthcare investing, driven by my passion for innovation in mental and behavioral health. I was a founding member of both the Health Assurance team and the Health Assurance Transformation Company (HATCo), a strategic platform that will own and operate a health system.

I partner with companies at the earliest stages across the US and India, as well as those transforming health systems. I am on the board of, or actively involved with, companies such as Commure, Transcarent, Loop Health, Orange Health, Cartwheel, Fay, HealthEx, Story Health, and several unannounced ventures.
I hold an A.B. from Harvard University and an M.B.A. from Harvard Business School. Outside of work, I enjoy traveling, (almost) any outdoor activity, and refining my culinary skills.

rows.name: Richard Will
lines: I am a Wealth Manager at GC Wealth, focused on pre-liquidity planning strategies and managing disciplined investment portfolios emphasizing tax efficiency, liquidity, and transparency. I am based in Jackson, WY.

Prior to joining General Catalyst, I was a founding employee of First Republic’s introduction to Jackson, WY in early 2019. I began my career in Chicago with RMB Capital Management and worked as a portfolio manager for First Western Trust. I graduated from the University of Denver, Daniels College of Business, and competed as a Division I NCAA athlete.
Outside of work, I enjoy hunting, fishing, skiing, and golfing with my wife Salem and dog Karl, while somehow finding the time and energy to coach the Jackson Hole High School lacrosse team.

rows.name: Riley Yang
lines: I am a senior analyst at GC Wealth, providing holistic investment and risk management solutions for entrepreneurs, executives, and their families. I construct customized investment portfolios to meet clients' unique needs, including income generation, capital appreciation, philanthropic objectives, and generational wealth transfer. I focus on all asset classes including equities, fixed income, alternatives, and private equity/venture.
I bring 12+ years of experience from J.P. Morgan, First Republic Bank, UBS, and AllianceBernstein, where I worked primarily with high-net worth clients based in the Bay Area.

I am based in San Francisco and graduated from UC Berkeley with degrees in Economics and Applied Mathematics. I am a Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA) charterholder. In my free time, I enjoy golf, basketball, and biking across the Golden Gate Bridge.

rows.name: Ripley Hartmeyer
lines: I lead General Catalyst's AI, Enterprise, Fintech, and Consumer talent efforts, partnering closely with founders and key stakeholders on talent strategy through all their phases of growth, from inception to exit. I also spend meaningful time proactively building out relevant operator, board member, advisor, and future founder networks, with a particular focus on AI.

Prior to GC, I led talent and community at Canvas Ventures, where I partnered with early-stage founders across enterprise, fintech, and healthcare. Before my career in venture capital, I served as a member of Spencer Stuart's Board, CEO, and Technology practices, focusing on global board and cross-functional executive searches for pre-IPO and publicly traded companies. I started my career in sales, operations, and project management, helping build two startups in risk management and cybersecurity before their successful exits.

I earned a Bachelor of Arts degree, majoring in Philosophy, Politics, Economics, and Law (PPEL), from the University of Richmond, where I co-captained their Division 1 women's tennis team. I grew up playing almost a dozen sports and learned many lessons now core to who I am on a court, course, field, and rink. Outside of work, I play competitive tennis, squash, and golf, and sign up for adventurous pursuits like running a marathon or climbing Mt. Kilimanjaro. I serve on the Board of Directors for the Glen Cove Boys & Girls Club and am passionate about mentoring youth in underserved communities and charitable causes focused on animal welfare and clean water.

rows.name: Robin Dechant
lines: At General Catalyst, I'm driving our resilience thesis in Europe with a focus on seed investing. I'm curious about technology and how it can solve our biggest problems in the physical world. Besides seed investing, I'm interested in exploring incubations and other creative strategies to shape industries such as manufacturing, energy, and defense.

I started my career at p9 capital investing in software and marketplaces. Later I became an entrepreneur, founding a field service software company for renewable energy installers that was acquired by Kraken Technologies (part of Octopus Energy). Following the acquisition, I've led the global implementation team for Kraken's field product line, working with utilities on modernizing their enterprise software stack. My own founder experience has fueled my passion for working with founders at the earliest stages, which eventually led me to angel investing.

I studied industrial engineering and management at the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology. Outside of work, I'm an avid ultra trail runner and have competed in races across the globe, including multiple crossings of the Alps on foot.

rows.name: Rohan Munsif
lines: I'm a Senior Analyst at GC Wealth, where I partner with clients to build personalized investment solutions through portfolio construction, investment analysis, and research. I focus on areas including liquidity planning, managing concentrated stock positions, and comprehensive balance sheet management.

I bring a decade of experience to GC Wealth. Most recently, I built portfolios with clients as an Investment Associate at J.P. Morgan and, prior to that, helped develop tailored investment strategies as an Associate Director at First Republic Private Wealth Management. I began my career at AllianceBernstein, a global asset management and wealth management firm.

My foundation is rooted in a quantitative background, holding a degree in Financial Mathematics and Statistics from the University of California, Santa Barbara, and I am a Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA) Charterholder. This quantitative foundation, combined with my experience working with clients ranging from founders, executives, and early-stage employees to families, allows me to deliver institutional-grade analysis while maintaining a personal approach to each client's unique objectives.
Outside of work, I stay active through skiing and playing sports like basketball and golf. I also volunteer at The Peninsula College Fund, where I mentor first-generation college students.

rows.name: Ron Paulus
lines: Ronald A. Paulus, MD, is Catalyst Advisor with General Catalyst and a Senior Scholar in the Stanford Clinical Excellence Research Center. He also serves as  President and CEO of RAPMD Strategic Advisors, providing advisory services to  health system Boards, CEOs and tech companies and as President of Maribel Health,  a General Catalyst company with a mission to make the home the center of the health  system. In addition, he has held numerous Board positions, including:  CoverMyMeds, Karius, Mercy, Olive, Ossium Health and PathAI.

Dr. Paulus was the immediate past President and CEO of Mission Health, a $2 billion integrated health  system serving all of western North Carolina -- a region older, poorer, sicker and less likely to be  insured than state and national averages. Mission Health included: six general acute care hospitals  (including four Critical Access Hospitals), a rehabilitation hospital, more than five hundred employed  providers, inpatient and home hospice programs, a PACE program and an MSSP Accountable Care  Organization comprised of more than 1,000 physicians in a region-wide clinically-integrated network.  Mission joined HCA Healthcare (HCA) in February 2019.

During his tenure, Mission Health reduced inpatient mortality by more than half, achieved six-sigma  medication safety results, improved patient experience to above the 90tpercentile, doubled employee  engagement scores to more than twice the national average and became the only health system ever designated as one of the nation’s Top 15 Health Systems for six of seven six years (IBM Watson Health,  2012-2018) performing in the top 2% of the United States in the last award period. Mission Health  closed a transformative transaction with HCA on February 1, 2019 creating the largest per capita  Foundation in America. The new $1.7+ billion Dogwood Health Trust is dedicated to impacting the  social determinants of health to dramatically improve the health and wellbeing of all peoples and  communities in western North Carolina.

Before joining Mission Health, Dr. Paulus was Executive Vice President, Clinical Operations and Chief Innovation Officer for Geisinger Health System, where he managed Geisinger’s hospitals and its more  than 800 physician member group practice and also was responsible for ensuring system-wide innovation. Prior to joining Geisinger, Dr. Paulus was co-founder, President and later CEO of  CareScience, Inc. (a NASDAQ company), later acquired by Premier, Inc. (NASDAQ: PINC;) providing an analytics platform to support health systems’ quality and efficiency improvement work used today  by nearly 1,000 hospitals nationwide.

Dr. Paulus received his MD degree from The School of Medicine, University of Pennsylvania, and his  MBA, concentration in healthcare management, and BS in Economics from The Wharton School,  University of Pennsylvania. He has published peer-reviewed book chapter and journal articles  (including in the Annals of Internal Medicine, New England Journal of Medicine and Health Affairs),  and speaks regularly on the topics of health care quality and efficiency, innovation, physician and  health system leadership and new models of care. Dr. Paulus has testified before both the US House  (on the 340b Drug Program) and the US Senate (the Stark and anti-kickback laws) and he has been  named one of Modern Healthcare’s Top 50 Most Influential Physician Executives and Leaders several  times, and was recently among the Top 15 on that list.
rows.title: Catalyst Advisor

rows.name: Roy Mabrey
lines: I am an investor at General Catalyst, focused on helping growth companies scale efficiently with the Customer Value Fund. I leverage my wide variety of operational leadership experiences at a variety of growth companies prior to GC.

Most recently, I ran Scope Security, a cybersecurity company focused on protecting the data and patients of health systems. Prior to Scope, I reignited Palantir's commercial healthcare business, building new partnerships with a variety of pharmaceutical companies and large payors. While at Palantir, I also led strategic finance efforts, interacting with the company's investors, board of directors, and financial planning efforts through its IPO.

Before Palantir, I was the CEO of Lifefactory, a consumer products company, where I led the company through a period of 10x revenue growth and product expansion prior to its sale to Thermos. I joined Lifefactory from Greenhouse Capital, an early investor in the company, where, in addition to sourcing new investments, I worked directly with Greenhouse's portfolio companies on cash management, fundraising, and growth plans.

I played college hockey at Amherst College, where I graduated with a BA. On weekends, you can find me at the soccer fields watching my two young daughters compete or at the local CrossFit gym trying to relive my past athletic accomplishments.

rows.name: Ryan Doherty
lines: I am a Director on our Investor Relations team, based in Cambridge, MA.

Prior to rejoining GC, I spent time as a senior manager in Fund and Portfolio Analytics at Omega Funds in Boston, where I worked to improve the firm’s data structure and integrity and supported their fundraising, financial operations, new investments, exit modeling, and reporting efforts.

My GC experience spans nearly four years, having joined as a finance associate in May 2018 and then promoted to portfolio operations manager in July 2020. From building models to track portfolio and related pacing rates, to helping migrate our portfolio companies’ data to the cloud, to owning the data room and data requests for our fundraising team, I’ve been closely involved in GC’s efforts across the investment process and have deep institutional knowledge.
I earned a B.S. in Computer Engineering with a minor in Business from Northeastern University.

rows.name: Samantha Van Gent
lines: When I collaborate with a founder, I'm energized by their passion for driving meaningful change and their commitment to building a sustainable and enduring company. I have always enjoyed working in communications, helping innovators navigate the complex world of PR, from strategizing how to tell compelling stories within ever-changing news cycles to nailing the tactics of executing a robust announcement.

I kick-started my career in the fast-paced world of public relations agencies, where I played a pivotal role in shaping communication strategies for startups, VC firms, and corporate giants. With a diverse clientele that included household names as well as up-and-coming innovators, I honed my skills across a spectrum of industries. I eventually found my drive in startup PR, working closely with founders as they grasped the importance of clear messaging and the power of building relationships with the press.

There is no better feeling than to get a note from a founder on how a story helped them hire new team members or how a well-positioned quote got picked up on social media or led to an invitation to speak at a conference. I’m so grateful to be on their journey and enjoy celebrating all of their PR wins.
Outside of work, I can be found hiking in Marin, planning my family’s next travel adventure, or happily hunting down the newest gems in San Francisco’s culinary scene.

rows.name: Samuel Beyer
lines: At General Catalyst, I focus on driving our early-stage venture business in Europe, co-conspiring with the most ambitious founders from day zero of their company-building journeys. I’m particularly drawn to entrepreneurs who see the world differently - those with the conviction, care, and creativity to turn novel market perspectives into enduring impact.

My fascination with this stage is deeply rooted in my own past. Having grown up in a small town in Germany with limited perspective, I developed a strong appreciation for opportunity and the people who create it. After working my way through education and earning two master’s degrees from the University of St. Gallen, I joined a venture in its early innings to help build its commercial foundation. Working alongside exceptional entrepreneurs, I came to see the 0-to-1 phase as the most formative chapter of any company’s life - where differentiated insight, relentless execution, and strong partnership turn ideas into real momentum.

Venture capital became a natural extension of that work, allowing me to partner with founders at the very beginning of their journeys time and again. I began investing at La Famiglia, a pure-play seed fund, and continue this mission today at General Catalyst.
When I’m not chasing the next great founder, I enjoy hunting down hidden food gems from the saddle of my old racing bike.

rows.name: Sara Chehrehsa
lines: I am an associate general counsel at General Catalyst. I am based in GC’s San Francisco office.
Prior to joining GC, I was a managing associate at Orrick, Herrington & Sutcliffe LLP in their technology companies group, where I represented various venture capital firms and startup companies.
I received a J.D. from Boston College Law School and a BA in Psychology from Princeton University.

rows.name: Sarah Joshi
lines: I am a Senior Associate at GC Wealth, based in San Francisco.

I leverage my expertise to oversee all operational, management, and day to day activities for our ultra high net worth families. I serve as their primary point of contact, managing all aspects of the financial relationship to ensure a seamless and personalized experience.

Prior to joining GC Wealth, I spent two years at First Republic and two years at JP Morgan, where I honed my skills in wealth management and client service. I hold a bachelor's degree in Economics from UC Berkeley and am a Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA) charterholder. In my free time, I stay active with tennis, skiing, and Pilates and love traveling to new places.

rows.name: Sarah McDonald
lines: I lead General Catalyst’s Healthcare Executive Talent efforts, supporting our portfolio companies with their leadership strategies, and building strategic networks throughout the healthcare ecosystem and beyond. My work centers on collaborating with visionary founders & CEOs who are creating breakthrough healthcare solutions, and I’m energized by the opportunity to bridge exceptional executive talent with the innovators who are reshaping how we deliver and experience care.

Before joining GC, I spent over six years at Daversa Partners, a leading retained executive search firm for venture backed tech companies. Throughout my tenure, I placed VP & C-Suite executives across enterprise and consumer tech companies. I ultimately focused on our healthcare practice, working closely with early and growth staged businesses as they made key hires across all functions on their leadership teams. Earlier in my career, I worked at the Advisory Board Company and supported our largest health system clients.
I graduated from the University of Virginia with a degree in Cognitive Science and Spanish. Based in NYC, you can find me reading or running Central Park during my spare time.

rows.name: Scott Lee
lines: I am a Senior Analyst on the GC Wealth team at General Catalyst, where I focus on trading, private investments, and reporting within the investment organization. I work with teams across the firm to drive efficiency, transparency, and insight across our investment operations.
Prior to joining GC Wealth, I worked at J.P. Morgan in equities and derivatives trading, portfolio trading, and reporting. Earlier in my career, I worked in FX and enterprise risk roles in Australia.
Originally from Sydney, Australia, I hold a Bachelor of Engineering in Aerospace Engineering from the University of New South Wales and a Graduate Diploma in Data Science from Monash University.

rows.name: Shelter Wein
lines: I am a Wealth Manager at GC Wealth, a next-generation wealth management platform built for transformational individuals, families, and organizations and a critical component of GC’s endeavor to go Beyond Venture. I am based in Jackson, Wyoming.

Prior to joining GC, I was a Preferred Banker at First Republic, supporting the holistic client experience, including banking, lending, and wealth management. From my multi-faceted role, I developed meaningful relationships through a deep understanding of client needs and an obsession with providing extraordinary service.

I graduated from Connecticut College with a BA (honors) in Psychology and a Minor in Chinese language and literature. I spent my summers and free time conducting research with professors, volunteering in group homes, and playing for the Women’s Water Polo Team. I am always looking for a pick-up game, which has been difficult to find in Wyoming. Instead of the pool, my dog Doug and I find ourselves skiing, biking, or hiking the trails of Teton Valley. I also dedicate my time to supporting local women mentoring and youth and family services focused on mental health.

rows.name: Siddhant Dubey
lines: I’m Siddhant, and I’m on the investment team at General Catalyst, India, focusing on early-stage software and AI across enterprise SaaS, dev tools, physical AI, hardware, and inference.

Before venture, I started building early. Pre-college, I founded Aahar, a platform to redistribute surplus food, which grew into one of India’s largest food redistribution network across 60+ cities before being acquired by JITO. That experience shaped my understanding of building and scaling in resource-constrained environments.

Post-college, I joined the founding team of an early-stage startup in Palo Alto as a machine learning engineer. My role quickly expanded across product, GTM, sales, and fundraising, as we scaled from 0 to $5M ARR in two years. It gave me a ground-up view of how companies are built in the Valley.

Returning to India was a deliberate choice to combine my experience in technology and Silicon Valley pattern recognition with on-ground insight into building in emerging markets. I aim to bring that operator perspective into investing, not just capital.
I studied at IIT Delhi. Outside work, I’m a national-level tennis player, enjoy all racket sports, love thrillers, and am a lifelong Messi and Barcelona fan.

rows.name: Sophia Han
lines: I lead our technical talent initiatives with a focus on our seed and early-stage portfolio at General Catalyst. Having the right talent is the key to success at the best companies, and I’m passionate about helping builders build from the very beginning.

Previously, I’ve operated in house at companies of different stages across both consumer and SAAS, from a large scale public one like Meta to hyper growth private ones like Brex and Quince. I primarily focus on technical hiring and have scaled technical orgs (engineering, product management, product design) from 15 people to 600+. I’ve also had the opportunity to build globally beyond the US, and have hired teams in Canada, Brazil, Israel, and China.

I graduated from UC Berkeley with a Business degree from the Haas School of Business and am based in the Bay Area. Outside of work, I enjoy discovering new restaurants for delicious food and taking agility classes with my dog. I’m also an avid traveler and am always looking to see new parts of the world.

rows.name: Stephen Klasko
lines: I’m a transformative leader and advocate for revolutionizing healthcare and higher education systems. After spending nine years in Philadelphia re-imagining the future of Jefferson, I’m now pursuing my vision of creatively reconstructing healthcare to address health inequities.

As president of Thomas Jefferson University and CEO of Jefferson Health from 2013 to 2021, I led one of the nation’s fastest-growing academic health institutions, built on my vision of re-imagining both healthcare and higher education.

Under my leadership, Jefferson expanded from three hospitals to 18 and grew from a health sciences university to a professional university with multiple campuses. Its revenue increased from $1.8 billion to $9 billion. A significant milestone was the 2017 merger of Thomas Jefferson University with Philadelphia University, creating a preeminent national doctoral university. This included top-20 programs in fashion and design and occupational therapy, the first design-thinking curriculum in a medical school, and the nation’s leading research on empathy in healthcare.

My success has earned me recognition, including being named Modern Healthcare’s #2 in 2018’s “100 Most Influential Individuals,” #21 in Fast Company’s “100 Most Creative People in Business 2018,” “Philadelphia Entrepreneur of the Year 2018,” Ernst & Young’s “Greater Philadelphia Entrepreneur of the Year 2018,” and Becker’s Hospital Review’s “100 Great Leaders in Healthcare.”

I’m also an internationally recognized advocate for transformation in healthcare and higher education. I co-authored UnHealthcare: A Manifesto for Health Assurance with Silicon Valley investor Hemant Taneja in 2020. In 2019, I spoke at the World Economic Forum in Davos about the future of hospitals, and in 2020, I was named a Distinguished Fellow of the World Economic Forum and co-chair of its Board of Stewards for the Forum's platform on the digital economy.
Before becoming President and CEO at Jefferson, I served as dean of two medical colleges and led three academic health centers.
I’m married to Colleen Wyse, a fashion leader and founder of The Philadelphia Trunk Show, and we have three children: Lynne, David, and Jill.
rows.title: Catalyst Advisor

rows.name: Steven Nichols
lines: I joined General Catalyst because I believe in our mission of Responsible Innovation. I have spent over a decade at the forefront of Sustainable Finance, raising hundreds of billions in capital for companies and projects that sit at the intersection of profit and purpose. Here at GC, I get to continue that work by supporting some of the most impactful companies we've invested in.

Before joining GC I built and ran the Sustainable Capital Markets franchise in the Americas region for Bank of America Securities. My team and I helped corporate issuers such as American Express, MasterCard, Salesforce, and Verizon raise over $300 billion in capital to support their investments that have positive environmental and/or social impact. I helped create groundbreaking innovations such as the first Sustainable IPO, the first sustainability-linked bond, and the first Equality Progress Sustainability Bonds. We ranked #1 in Sustainable Capital Markets league tables every year, and Bank of America was named the 2022 Americas ESG Financing House of the Year by International Financing Review (IFR). I had the honor of representing Bank of America on the Executive Committee of the Green and Social Bond Principles, a global body which maintains guidance referenced by 97% of issuers in the $7 trillion impact-themed bond market.

Prior to joining BofA, I held corporate finance and Treasury roles in the airline and electric utility industries. In 2015, I led a $1 billion Green Bond offering for Southern Company, becoming one of the first Green Bond issuers globally, and helping lay the foundation for impact-oriented capital markets as we know them today.

I earned a B.S. in Management from Georgia Tech and an MBA from Chicago Booth. I have attended 5 FIFA World Cups and run a small social media account dedicated to covering US Soccer. I am based in my hometown of Atlanta where I get to golf 12 months a year on some great courses, travel practically anywhere in the world on a non-stop flight, and help build this city's improving innovation ecosystem.
rows.title: Managing Director

rows.name: Tanya Dutta
lines: I lead our talent efforts for the India market, closely supporting our portfolio companies and cultivating relevant solid networks across various sectors. I'm excited by General Catalyst's vision for investing and transformation in the region and building on the same from a strategic talent perspective. At my last role as AVP, Human Capital at Z47, I worked closely with early stage founders focussing on proactively finding them their next best hire! Prior to which I was part of Global Talent Acquisition teams at PayU and OYO. I started my career with a Global Boutique search firm, Positive Moves. I hold a Master in Organization and Social Psychology from London School of Economics and a Honors Degree in Psychology from Delhi University. I hail from Delhi, India, am trained in Kathak, a classical Indian dance form, and recently started practicing Yoga, which I believe does wonders for the mind and body. I also am a devoted plant parent and have an inside joke that one of my plants would thrive so much one day it will be ready to apply to a top university. Finally, I'm a food enthusiast, weekends and vacations are all about trying new cuisines and restaurants. "Live to eat" is my motto.

rows.name: Thomas Mathew
lines: I am the Co-founder & CTO of Percepta (a GC Transformation Company). I lead all software development, technical execution, and architecture development as we aim to transform the world’s businesses.

Prior to GC, I was a founding engineer at Credal, and before that, I spent eight years as an engineer at Palantir. My proudest accomplishments have centered around 0-1 product development, especially when tied to a strong mission with large-scale impact. At Palantir, that included leading a team to develop the product used to report key metrics to the White House during the height of the Covid pandemic, enabling the nation’s top leaders to track critical data like hospitalization rates and vaccine rollout statistics.
Earlier in my career, I developed software at Citadel and Bloomberg. I earned my bachelor’s degree in mathematics and computer science from the University of Michigan.

Outside of work, I love cooking - especially overly elaborate South Asian meals - and immersive travel. I’ve lived on five continents for over a year each and is still working on Australia and Antarctica.
rows.title: Co-founder & CTO, Percepta

rows.name: Tia Sgouros
lines: As a Relationship Manager, I partner with clients to simplify the complexities of their financial lives. Based in Washington, DC, I am the primary liaison between our administrative and investment professionals, ensuring we deliver a personalized client experience centered on proactive communication, attention to detail, and unwavering trust. My focus is guiding high net worth individuals and families through the complexities of wealth structuring, estate planning, and tax-efficient strategies by partnering closely with our clients' legal and CPA teams.

My career in private wealth began while I was in college, interning each summer with my current team at Merrill Lynch. Upon graduating from Christopher Newport University's Luter School of Business with a B.A. in Finance and a minor in Leadership, I joined the team as a Client Service Associate at First Republic/J.P. Morgan, a role that provided me with the critical knowledge and experience to deliver exceptional service.

Outside of the office, I enjoy watching classical ballet performances, since I spent 14 years in a pre-professional, Vaganova style ballet program. I'm always seeking new experiences, from exploring new countries to taking my annual summer trip to visit my family in Greece.

rows.name: Tony Ho
lines: I discovered my love of math and computer science at an early age and began entering competitions in those fields for the pure enjoyment of breaking down puzzles and solving them at speed. While studying applied math and computer science at Harvard, I aced a hackathon and won a position coding for a newly launched tech recruiting firm before I was out of college. I quickly realized that while building a young business also demanded fast, accurate problem-solving, the results made a difference in the real world.

I took my skills and experience into one of the more results-sensitive industries out there – media and entertainment – as CTO for Los Angeles-based EDO, which uses data to assess and predict the effectiveness of marketing for movies, television, and online media. As I note, the entertainment industry is like venture investing: it’s hard to predict the winners, but better information almost always improves the odds.

I came to the venture side as director of engineering for an early-stage firm seeking to incorporate data into the day-to-day work of supporting portfolio companies on their growth journey. With General Catalyst, I lead the engineering on Customer Value Fund – a source of capital underwritten by a company’s cohorts and cash flows. Part of working with CVF involves analyzing company data from a completely different angle.
On my own time, I’m a fan of the Golden State Warriors and a consumer of all media. I also find time to inspire young people to pursue their love of math and science.

rows.name: Tracy Fong
lines: At General Catalyst, I lead fund-partnership investments, where I focus on engaging, sourcing, supporting, and investing in seed and emerging fund managers within the venture capital ecosystem.

Before joining General Catalyst, I spent 25+ years in startups and technology firms and 20+ years as an institutional allocator across various alternative and traditional asset classes. I began investing in emerging managers in 2010 and have been actively investing in technology companies since 2004.
