Earlier, I worked at Albourne Partners, SVB Capital, Harvard Management Company, Yahoo!, and startups in 1999-2000, Varsity Books and Webvan. I am a graduate of the University of California (B.S. in Business Administration) and Harvard Business School (MBA).
rows.title: Partner, Fund-Partnerships

rows.name: Tyler Olkowski
lines: At General Catalyst, I focus on partnering with founders at the earliest stages as a member of the Health Assurance team. I love working with founders as they grapple with turning an idea into an enduring business, particularly when that idea has the potential to make our world a better place.

After toying with a career in journalism or public policy, I began my career on J.P. Morgan’s Not-For-Profit Healthcare team, working with hospitals to raise capital and pursue strategic initiatives. I then joined Savvy, a YC-backed seed-stage startup at the intersection of healthcare and insurtech, where I touched just about everything aside from the code base (go-to-market, customer onboarding and support, insurance enrollment and operations). I then began my investing career at Greycroft, where I was able to work closely with founders across healthcare and the life sciences.

I joined General Catalyst to help achieve the mission of transforming healthcare from a “sick care” system to a proactive system that helps people stay well while bending the cost curve. I’m excited to be surrounded by and work with mission-driven investors, who understand technology’s ability to improve the world and are committed to backing healthcare’s most impactful businesses.
Outside of work, I enjoy running, watching Notre Dame Football, and walking (admittedly sometimes dragging) our miniature long-haired dachshund, Penelope, around NYC with my wife, Meg.

rows.name: Vedant Suri
lines: Born into a family with strong entrepreneurial roots, I immigrated to Canada from India at a young age. Observing my parents build their lives in a new environment instilled in me the importance of grit, tenacity, and a healthy dose of irreverence for the status quo. I attended the Ivey Business School in Canada, where I studied cognitive neuroscience and finance. My goal was to understand how complex systems work and to gain a deeper appreciation for how both people and companies adapt and grow.

Completing summer internships at Y Combinator, with Goldman Sachs, and spending time with budding entrepreneurs solidified my desire to help create and foster emerging companies. I made my move into investing with CapitalG (Alphabet's growth investment fund), where I focused on investments in B2B SaaS and data infrastructure. Prior to this, I spent a number of years with the Boston Consulting Group, primarily in the technology and private equity arenas.

At General Catalyst, I focus on enterprise software across stages and am passionate about product-led software companies led by founders who have a deep understanding of the problems they're solving. I chose the firm in part because of its rich heritage of working closely with founders and management teams. I consider it a great privilege to be a partner to teams navigating the ups and downs of company building.

My love of travel has taken me to more than 40 countries, with my most recent adventure being an 85-mile trek in Patagonia. I root for Chelsea in the English Premier League, enjoy smooth jazz, and give back to my community in accordance with the Sanskrit term “seva,” or selfless service.

rows.name: Wes Peltzman
lines: I'm VP, Compliance & Regulatory Counsel at General Catalyst, where I focus on SEC compliance, conflicts management and fund formation work as GC scales and expands. This work has been a throughline of my career; it sits at the intersection of capital formation, regulation, and the operating mechanics that let a great firm run, and GC is a transformational place to do it.

My path here was not linear. Before law school, I joined Lattice as their first full-time employee, working in customer operations and business development. That experience taught me what it takes to build a company from the ground up. I later went in-house at a registered investment adviser, where I helped lead legal and compliance work across the fund platform. Most recently, I was at Cooley LLP in the fund formation group, advising venture funds and fund-of-funds on fundraising and formation matters. While there, I also helped lead a cross-functional team that implemented AI tools across the firm. That back-and-forth between law firm and operator seats shaped how I work today; I bring outside-counsel rigor with the pragmatism of someone who has sat on the business side.

What drew me to GC is how the firm approaches its work: with calculated aspirations, relentless curiosity, and a focus on helping the people around us succeed. I see compliance through that same lens, as a path to supporting transformation rather than a back-end review function. The best compliance work is built into how a firm operates and iterates, earning trust and helping the founders and partners we serve.
I earned my J.D. from the University of Pennsylvania Carey Law School and my B.A. in Communications from the University of Maryland.
Outside of work, you'll usually find me hiking with my wife and our two large rescue dogs, whose insatiable energy keeps us all moving. I love live music, comedy, and Philly sports. Go Birds!

rows.name: Will Walker
lines: I currently serve as the Vice President of Defense Industrial Policy at the General Catalyst Institute, where I work with founders and policymakers to strengthen the American industrial base and advance our national resilience through transformative technologies.
I grew up in Southern Appalachia and came of age around 9/11, as our nation and its Allies went to war. An Army ROTC scholarship took me to The Citadel, where I commissioned as an infantry officer.

I spent the next eleven years in the Army, leading infantry and special operations formations, with combat and operational deployments across South Asia and Eastern Europe. I worked alongside diplomats and intelligence professionals, and came to value teams that bring different perspectives to hard problems.

That work eventually brought me to Washington, D.C., and deeper into national security. I later studied international public policy at Johns Hopkins SAIS, where I researched how emerging and disruptive technologies are changing the character of war and reshaping America’s strategic competition.

I wanted to work more directly with the people building those technologies and the national security professionals putting them to use. At Onebrief, I established the company’s first international vertical, working with U.S. Allies and partners as they adapted to a rapidly changing technological and security environment. I later established Onebrief’s federal vertical, working directly with the Office of the Secretary of War, the Intelligence Community, homeland security organizations, and other federal agencies.

Curiosity carries through most parts of my life, from traveling and being outdoors to art, history, languages, and staying active. Most of all, I value time with family and friends, and remaining connected to and supporting the military, veteran, and national security communities that have given me so much.

rows.name: Yuri Sagalov
lines: I can pinpoint the exact moment in time I fell in love with technology. I was six years old and my parents brought home a borrowed 386 with a black/green screen and a copy of Prince of Persia. My first programming language was Logo, and my first "real" programming language was C. As I grew up, I always tinkered with computers, software, and later the internet. Eventually, in University I specialized in Computer Science, and ended up dropping out of grad school to come to the Bay Area, participate in Y Combinator, and start a startup in 2010. I ran that startup for about 7 years before it was acquired.

In 2014 I joined Y Combinator as a partner and spent 5 years there working with (and learning from) some of the smartest founders in the world. After YC I started my own fund, Wayfinder, where I worked hand in hand with founders from their earliest days. Through both Wayfinder and my own angel portfolio I've been fortunate to be able to invest in companies like Flexport, Supabase, Decagon, Legora, Browserbase, Vetcove, Verse Medical, and dozens others.
At General Catalyst I lead our seed strategy, partnering with founders at the earliest stages of their journey — often before they’ve even incorporated.
I graduated from the University of Toronto with a Bachelor of Applied Science focusing on Computer and Software Engineering.
Outside of work I enjoy flying airplanes, sailing in the bay, and spending time with my 2 year old.
rows.title: Managing Director

rows.name: Zeynep Yavuz-Willson
lines: I am a Partner at General Catalyst, focused on founders who have an outsider mentality, deep ambition, and think creatively from day one - particularly in underserved markets and sectors ripe for transformation.

Watching my entrepreneur parents build a technology company in Turkey without access to venture capital taught me two things: that brilliant founders exist everywhere, and that capital scarcity often breeds the most creative problem-solving. That's why I became an investor focused on markets and founders that traditional VC often ignores.

I began my career in technology investment banking at Merrill Lynch in New York, before moving to the investing side at TA Associates, a global growth equity fund, in London. There, I learned how to build trust with entrepreneurs from diverse backgrounds and nationalities, many of whom had never considered outside capital as a catalyst for growth.

Working closely with founders also made me realize the importance of operating experience in being a truly effective partner. To build that perspective, I stepped away from investing and joined the product team at ZEPZ, where I learned how to run product teams at speed and launch products in emerging markets that leapfrog traditional incumbent systems.

While Europe is my base, I work with companies globally. At General Catalyst, I work with founders from the earliest stages of company formation through later-stage growth. Much of my investing focuses on applying technology and first-principles thinking to reimagine traditional business models and drive structural industry transformation.

I grew up in a city nestled between the mountains and the sea, which is why adventure sports feel like home to me. I love hiking, skiing, open-water swimming, and kitesurfing - and I'm always up for trying new adventure sports in nature.
